definition_zh: 联赛；联盟；同盟；（旧）结盟
definition_en: a group of sports teams that compete against one another, an alliance of states or groups, and an older verb meaning to unite in such an alliance
core_image: 一排球队队旗插在同一块场地上，旗与旗之间用绳子系在一起
scene: 赛季开始前，球迷在球场外排起长队。Their team finished top of the league last season.
sceneCN: 这里 league 指「联赛」（第 1 个义项）；句意为他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。图中可辨识物件：队旗、球场看台、积分榜。

derivatives.zh: 由 league 与 table 复合，指联赛积分榜
由 non- 加 league 构成，指不属于职业联赛的
league 的复数形式，也可指很远的距离，如 leagues away

senses.title: A group of teams competing against each other
senses.definition: an organized group of sports clubs or teams that play against one another for a title
senses.definitionCN: 为争夺冠军而相互比赛的有组织的体育俱乐部或队伍
senses.example: Their team finished top of the league last season.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。
senses.why: A league was first a group bound by an agreement, and teams bound into a fixture list are exactly that: a set of rivals tied to the same schedule.
senses.whyCN: league 最初指由协议绑在一起的一群人，而被赛程绑在一起的球队正是如此：一群被同一张日程拴住的对手。

senses.title: An alliance of states or groups
senses.definition: an association of countries, parties or groups formed to act together
senses.definitionCN: 为共同行动而组成的国家、政党或团体联合体
senses.example: Several small states formed a league to protect their trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 几个小国结成联盟以保护各自的贸易路线。
senses.why: Latin ligare means to bind, so the political sense is the literal one: separate parties tied by a treaty into one body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，所以政治义才是字面义：彼此独立的各方被条约绑成一个整体。

senses.title: To unite in an alliance
senses.definition: to join together with others in an alliance, now mainly literary or historical
senses.definitionCN: 与他人联合结成同盟，现在多用于文学或历史叙述
senses.example: The border towns leagued together against the raiders.
senses.exampleCN: 边境各镇联合起来对抗入侵者。
senses.why: If a league is a body bound together, then to league is simply to enter that binding, which is why the verb mirrors the noun.
senses.whyCN: 如果 league 是被绑在一起的整体，那么 to league 就是加入这次捆绑，因此动词与名词完全对应。

intro.en: League comes from a Latin verb meaning to bind, by way of Italian and French, so an alliance is literally a tying together.
intro.cn: league 经意大利语和法语来自拉丁语中意为「捆绑」的动词，所以同盟字面上就是「绑在一起」。

items.en: Ligare meant to bind or tie, and a league was first a binding together of people.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑、结合，而 league 最初指把人们绑在一起。

items.en: Italian lega named an alliance, a group bound by an agreement.
items.cn: 意大利语 lega 指同盟，即由协议绑在一起的一群人。

items.en: Old French ligue carried the political sense of a confederacy into English.
items.cn: 古法语 ligue 把「邦联、同盟」这一政治含义带进英语。

items.en: Middle English league named an alliance of rulers, and by the sixteenth century it also named a group of sports sides.
items.cn: 中古英语 league 指统治者之间的同盟，到十六世纪也指一组体育队伍。

items.en: Modern English keeps the alliance sense in phrases such as in league with, while the sports sense dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 现代英语在 in league with 等说法中保留同盟义，体育运动义则主导日常使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and compounds of league; the near-meaning group collects other words for an alliance.
note.cn: 形近组收 league 的形式与复合词；近义组收其他表示同盟的词。

entries.definition: The plural of league, for several competitions or alliances.
entries.definitionCN: league 的复数，指多个联赛或同盟。

entries.definition: The past form, meaning formed an alliance.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，意为结成了同盟。

entries.definition: Outside the professional league system, used of smaller clubs.
entries.definitionCN: 不属于职业联赛体系的，用于较小的俱乐部。

entries.definition: A formal agreement to work together.
entries.definitionCN: 正式约定共同行动的联盟。

entries.definition: A temporary union of parties or groups.
entries.definitionCN: 政党或团体组成的临时联合。

entries.definition: A union of states or organizations with shared rules.
entries.definitionCN: 按共同规则组成的国家或组织联合体。

entries.definition: The act or state of being joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 联合的行为或状态。

normalIntro.en: The word means a binding, and both a treaty and a fixture list are ways of tying separate parties into one arrangement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的意思是「捆绑」，而条约与赛程都是把彼此独立的一方绑进同一安排的方式。

normal.en: Latin ligare means to bind, so a league is people or teams tied together.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 意为捆绑，所以 league 就是被绑在一起的人或球队。

normal.en: The League of Nations was literally a binding of states after a war.
normal.cn: 国际联盟字面上就是战后各国的一次捆绑。

normal.en: In league with somebody usually hints at a secret or dishonest binding.
normal.cn: in league with somebody 通常暗示一种秘密或不正当的勾结。

normal.en: A football league is a binding by schedule: every club must play every other.
normal.cn: 足球联赛是一种按赛程的捆绑：每个俱乐部都必须与其他俱乐部比赛。

normal.en: To league is the old verb for entering that alliance, now mostly literary.
normal.cn: to league 是表示加入同盟的旧动词，现在多用于文学。

abstract.en: Competition and alliance share one word because both require parties to accept the same set of obligations.
abstract.cn: 竞争与同盟共用一个词，因为两者都要求各方接受同一套义务。

abstract.en: A league is a promise made visible: the table, the fixture list, the treaty are its rope.
abstract.cn: 联赛是把承诺变得可见：积分榜、赛程、条约就是它的绳子。

abstract.en: To be in league is to be tied to someone, whether by trust or by guilt.
abstract.cn: 身处一个 league 就是与某人绑在一起，不论靠信任还是靠罪责。

examples.en: Their team finished top of the league last season.
examples.cn: 他们的球队上赛季排名联赛榜首。

examples.en: Several small states formed a league to protect their trade routes.
examples.cn: 几个小国结成联盟以保护各自的贸易路线。

examples.en: The border towns leagued together against the raiders.
examples.cn: 边境各镇联合起来对抗入侵者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离格」——离了格的球队被编进同一个联赛；谐音记住 league 是联赛、联盟。

root: 源自拉丁语 ligare（捆绑），经意大利语 lega 与古法语 ligue 进入英语；同盟本义即「绑在一起」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a binding of separate parties; it appears as a political alliance, a sporting competition and the old verb for joining one.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把彼此独立的各方绑在一起；它表现为政治同盟、体育联赛，以及表示加入同盟的旧动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: club flags planted in one field, tied to each other with rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排队旗插在同一块场地上，旗与旗用绳子系在一起。

branches.en: envoys signing a treaty in a plain room
branches.cn: 使节在简朴的房间里签署条约

branches.en: small states joining to guard a trade road
branches.cn: 小国联合以守护贸易通道

branches.en: a table showing every club's points
branches.cn: 显示各俱乐部积分的积分榜

branches.en: a full stadium on a match day
branches.cn: 比赛日坐满的球场

branches.en: border towns swearing to stand together
branches.cn: 边境各镇宣誓共同抵御

intro.en: A Latin verb for binding passes through Italian and French, and English adds plural and compound forms to name competitions and alliances.
intro.cn: 一个表示捆绑的拉丁动词经意大利语与法语传来，英语又加复数与复合形式来命名联赛与同盟。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 漏；漏出；漏洞；泄露（秘密）
definition_en: to let liquid or gas escape through a hole; to give out secret information; a hole through which something escapes, or the information disclosed
core_image: 水管接缝处慢慢渗出的一滴水珠
scene: 厨房水管接头处渗出水来，地上很快积了一小片。A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
sceneCN: 这里是「漏出」（第 1 个义项：液体从孔洞中漏出）；句意是管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。图中可辨识物件：水管接头、水珠、地面的水迹。

derivatives.zh: 由 leak 加 -age 构成，义为「泄漏；泄漏量」
由 leak 加 -y 构成，义为「漏的；爱泄露的」
由 leak 加 -er 构成，义为「泄密者」

senses.title: To let liquid or gas escape
senses.definition: to let liquid or gas escape through a hole or crack
senses.definitionCN: 让液体或气体从孔洞、裂缝中跑出来
senses.example: A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
senses.exampleCN: 管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。
senses.why: The Middle English verb named a slow dripping escape, so the physical movement of liquid is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语的动词指缓慢滴漏地跑掉，所以液体实际的移动是最早的义项。

senses.title: A hole through which something escapes
senses.definition: a hole or crack through which liquid or gas escapes
senses.definitionCN: 液体或气体借以跑出的孔洞或裂缝
senses.example: The plumber finally found the leak behind the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 水管工终于在水槽后面找到了漏洞。
senses.why: If a thing leaks, the opening that allows the escape can take the same name, turning the action into the place where it happens.
senses.whyCN: 某物会漏，那么允许它跑出的开口也能用同一个名字，于是动作变成了动作发生的位置。

senses.title: To give out secret information
senses.definition: to give secret information to someone who should not have it
senses.definitionCN: 把秘密信息交给不该得到它的人
senses.example: Someone leaked the report to the press before it was published.
senses.exampleCN: 有人在报告发表前把它泄露给了媒体。
senses.why: Information escapes like liquid: once the barrier is broken, what was contained spreads beyond its intended boundary.
senses.whyCN: 信息像液体一样跑掉：一旦屏障破了，原本被盛住的东西就会扩散到不该去的地方。

senses.title: The secret information disclosed
senses.definition: the secret information that has been disclosed
senses.definitionCN: 被泄露出去的秘密信息
senses.example: The leak forced the minister to explain himself in public.
senses.exampleCN: 泄露的消息迫使部长公开作出解释。
senses.why: By the same shift as the hole, the noun can name the disclosed material rather than the act of disclosing it.
senses.whyCN: 和「漏洞」一样的转喻，名词可以指被泄露的内容，而不是泄露这个动作。

intro.en: Leak is a Germanic word of uncertain exact origin, probably related to Dutch and Norse verbs for dripping; English extended it from water to secrets.
intro.cn: leak 是日耳曼语词，确切来源不确定，很可能与荷兰语、古诺斯语中表示滴落的动词有关；英语把它从水扩展到秘密。

items.en: A Germanic source is generally assumed, but the exact reconstructed form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为源自日耳曼语，但确切的重构形式并不确定。

items.en: Middle Dutch leken meant to drip or to let liquid through.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 leken 意为滴下或让液体透过。

items.en: Old Norse leka carried a similar sense of running or dripping.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 leka 有相近的「流淌、滴落」之意。

items.en: Middle English leken named the slow escape of liquid from a container.
items.cn: 中古英语 leken 指液体从容器中慢慢漏出。

items.en: Modern English extended the verb to secrets, and made the noun mean both the hole and the disclosure.
items.cn: 现代英语把动词扩展到秘密，并让名词同时指漏洞与泄露的内容。

note.en: The look-alike group collects derivatives and one homophone; the near-meaning group collects verbs of liquid and secrets escaping.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词和一个同音词；近义组收表示液体或秘密跑掉的动词。

entries.definition: The act of leaking, or the amount that escapes.
entries.definitionCN: 泄漏；泄漏的量。

entries.definition: Letting liquid through; not watertight.
entries.definitionCN: 会漏的；不密封的。

entries.definition: A person who gives secret information to others.
entries.definitionCN: 向他人泄露秘密的人。

entries.definition: A long green vegetable related to the onion; it sounds the same but has a different history.
entries.definitionCN: 一种与洋葱近亲的长绿蔬菜；它与 leak 同音，但词源不同。

entries.definition: To fall in small drops, usually slowly.
entries.definitionCN: 以小滴形式缓慢落下。

entries.definition: To let liquid flow out of a container by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 意外让液体从容器中流出。

entries.definition: To get out of a place where something is held.
entries.definitionCN: 从被盛放或困住的地方跑出来。

entries.definition: To make secret information known.
entries.definitionCN: 使秘密信息为人所知。

normalIntro.en: The word starts with liquid finding a way out; its suffixes build the amount, the quality and the person, and one homophone is a vegetable.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从液体找到出口开始；它的后缀造出量、性质和人物，而一个同音词是蔬菜。

normal.en: Leak began with liquid escaping through a small opening, which is why every later sense keeps the idea of a breach.
normal.cn: leak 起初指液体从小口跑出，所以后来每个义项都保留「破口」的想法。

normal.en: Leakage adds -age and names the process or the amount, not the hole itself.
normal.cn: leakage 加 -age，指过程或数量，而不是孔洞本身。

normal.en: Leaky adds -y and turns the verb into an adjective: a leaky bucket is one that lets water through.
normal.cn: leaky 加 -y，把动词变成形容词：leaky bucket 就是会漏水的水桶。

normal.en: Leaker adds -er and names the person who lets information out.
normal.cn: leaker 加 -er，指把信息放出去的人。

normal.en: Leek is only a homophone: the vegetable's name has a different origin and nothing to do with dripping.
normal.cn: leek 只是同音词：这种蔬菜的名字来源不同，与滴漏无关。

abstract.en: Containers fail at their edges, and so do institutions, which is why a word for a hole serves for a secret.
abstract.cn: 容器常在边缘失效，机构也是如此，所以一个表示孔洞的词能用来指秘密。

abstract.en: What leaks is always something that was meant to stay inside, so the word carries a quiet accusation.
abstract.cn: 漏出的东西总是本该留在里面的东西，所以这个词带着一种安静的指责。

abstract.en: A single drop is enough to prove the barrier has failed, which is why leaks are found before they are measured.
abstract.cn: 一滴就足以证明屏障已经失效，所以人们总是先发现漏点，再去测量漏量。

examples.en: A small hole in the pipe let water leak into the basement.
examples.cn: 管子上的小孔让水漏进了地下室。

examples.en: Someone leaked the report to the press before it was published.
examples.cn: 有人在报告发表前把它泄露给了媒体。

examples.en: The plumber finally found the leak behind the sink.
examples.cn: 水管工终于在水槽后面找到了漏洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哩可」——水从缝里「哩可」一下跑出来；leak 是漏。

root: 日耳曼语来源，一般认为与中古荷兰语 leken、古诺斯语 leka（滴落、渗漏）有关；确切词源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core is liquid finding a way out; the senses divide into the opening, the disclosure of secrets and the disclosed material itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是液体找到出口；义项由此分为孔洞、秘密的泄露，以及被泄露的内容本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one drop forming at a pipe joint and falling to the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：水管接缝处凝成一滴水珠，落到地面。

branches.en: water finding a crack in an old pipe
branches.cn: 水在旧管子上找到一道裂缝

branches.en: a plumber's torch aimed behind a sink
branches.cn: 水管工的手电照向水槽后面

branches.en: a document passed to a journalist in secret
branches.cn: 一份文件被秘密交给记者

branches.en: a headline built from information that escaped
branches.cn: 用跑出来的信息做成的头条

branches.en: a wet floor under a joint that will not seal
branches.cn: 封不住的接头下方湿了一片地面

intro.en: A Germanic verb gains three English suffixes for amount, quality and person, while a homophone vegetable stays unrelated.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语动词加三个英语后缀，分别表示数量、性质和人物；同音的蔬菜词则并无关系。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

the act or amount of leaking

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀：具有某种性质

definition_zh: 跳跃；跃过；骤增
definition_en: to jump suddenly, to jump over something, or to increase sharply
core_image: 一个人屈膝蓄力，整个人腾空越过一道窄沟
scene: 河岸边的鹿受到惊吓，前腿一蹬便越过灌木。The deer leaped over the low hedge.
sceneCN: 这里是「跃过」（第 2 个义项：动词，指跳过某个障碍）；句意为鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。图中可辨识物件：河岸、受惊的鹿、低矮树篱。

derivatives.zh: 由 leap 与 frog 复合，义为「跳背游戏；蛙跳式超越」
由 leap 加 -er 构成，义为「跳跃者」
由 leap 加 -ing 构成，义为「跳跃的；跃动的」

senses.title: To jump suddenly
senses.definition: to move through the air by pushing off the ground with the legs
senses.definitionCN: 用腿蹬地、身体腾空移动
senses.example: The deer leaped over the low hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。
senses.why: Leap is an old Germanic verb for a springing movement, stronger and more sudden than the everyday jump.
senses.whyCN: leap 是古老的日耳曼动词，表示弹跳式的动作，比日常的 jump 更用力、更突然。

senses.title: To jump over an obstacle
senses.definition: to cross something by jumping over it
senses.definitionCN: 通过跳过去而越过某物
senses.example: He leaped the fence and ran into the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他跃过栅栏，跑进田里。
senses.why: Once the verb names the jump, the thing jumped over can become its direct object, so leap gains the sense of clearing an obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然表示跳，被跳过的东西就能作宾语，于是 leap 有了「越过障碍」的意思。

senses.title: To increase sharply
senses.definition: to rise suddenly and by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 突然且大幅度地上升
senses.example: Profits leaped in the second quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第二季度利润猛涨。
senses.why: A sharp rise looks like a jump on a graph, so the physical leap is borrowed for numbers that suddenly go up.
senses.whyCN: 陡升在图表上就像一次跳跃，于是身体的 leap 被借来形容数字的猛涨。

senses.title: A jump or a sharp rise
senses.definition: an act of jumping, or a sudden large increase
senses.definitionCN: 一次跳跃，或突然的大幅增长
senses.example: There was a leap in demand for electric cars.
senses.exampleCN: 电动汽车的需求出现了一次跃升。
senses.why: The noun simply names the event that the verb describes, whether in space or on a chart.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是给动词所描述的事件命名，无论在空间里还是在图表上。

intro.en: Leap is an Old English verb of springing, shared across the Germanic languages and unchanged in its central sense.
intro.cn: leap 是古英语中表示弹跳的动词，在日耳曼语族中广泛共享，核心义一直未变。

items.en: Hleapan meant to jump or spring, often with the image of pushing off the ground.
items.cn: hleapan 意为跳跃、弹起，常带有蹬地发力的画面。

items.en: The reconstructed *hlaupan is shared by German laufen, which shifted towards running.
items.cn: 重构形式 *hlaupan 为德语 laufen 所共享，后者词义转向「跑」。

items.en: Middle English lepen keeps the jump and adds the sense of jumping over something.
items.cn: 中古英语 lepen 保留跳跃义，并添上「跳过某物」的意思。

items.en: The figurative sense of a sudden rise appears in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 表示「突然上升」的比喻义在十七世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps both past forms, leaped and leapt, and uses leap year for the calendar's extra day.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 leaped 与 leapt 两种过去式，并用 leap year 指日历中多出的那一天。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and forms of leap; the near-meaning group gathers words for jumping and rising.
note.cn: 形近组收 leap 的复合词与变形；近义组收表示跳跃与上升的词。

entries.definition: A game of jumping over others, or to overtake by a jump.
entries.definitionCN: 跳背游戏；蛙跳式超越。

entries.definition: A person or animal that leaps.
entries.definitionCN: 跳跃者。

entries.definition: Moving with jumps.
entries.definitionCN: 跳跃的；跃动的。

entries.definition: The irregular past of leap.
entries.definitionCN: leap 的不规则过去式。

entries.definition: To push off and move through the air.
entries.definitionCN: 跳；跳跃。

entries.definition: A small jump on one leg or both.
entries.definitionCN: 单脚或双脚小跳。

entries.definition: A long, energetic jump.
entries.definitionCN: 大步跳跃。

entries.definition: A sudden large increase.
entries.definitionCN: 激增。

normalIntro.en: A short Germanic verb with two past forms, leap keeps its spring in space and lends it to numbers.
normalIntro.cn: 一个简短的日耳曼动词带有两种过去式，leap 把弹跳留在空间里，又借给数字。

normal.en: Leap has two past forms: leaped and leapt.
normal.cn: leap 有两种过去式：leaped 与 leapt。

normal.en: Leap over is the phrase for clearing an obstacle.
normal.cn: leap over 是表示越过障碍的搭配。

normal.en: Leap year takes its name from the extra day that makes the calendar jump.
normal.cn: leap year 得名于让日历「跳」一下的多余那一天。

normal.en: Leapfrog joins leap and frog, from a game of jumping over backs.
normal.cn: leapfrog 由 leap 与 frog 组合，来自跳过别人背部的游戏。

normal.en: Leap to conclusions means deciding without enough evidence.
normal.cn: leap to conclusions 意为没有足够证据就下结论。

abstract.en: A jump needs a firm push before it needs open air, which is why leap implies stored force.
abstract.cn: 跳跃先需要稳稳蹬地，才需要腾空，所以 leap 含着蓄力。

abstract.en: The same word describes a deer and a profit because both leave the ground suddenly.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能描述鹿，也能描述利润，因为二者都突然离开了原来的水平。

abstract.en: In a leap, the body is briefly between two places, belonging to neither.
abstract.cn: 在跳跃中，身体短暂处在两地之间，谁也不属于。

examples.en: The deer leaped over the low hedge.
examples.cn: 鹿跃过了低矮的树篱。

examples.en: Profits leaped in the second quarter.
examples.cn: 第二季度利润猛涨。

examples.en: There was a leap in demand for electric cars.
examples.cn: 电动汽车的需求出现了一次跃升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「力扑」——用力扑出去，就是 leap。

root: 古英语 hleapan（跳跃），与德语 laufen 同出日耳曼语族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a springing push-off; it extends from a jump to clearing an obstacle, then to a sharp rise and the increase itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是蹬地弹起；由跳跃扩展到越过障碍，再扩展到猛涨与那次增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body folded at the knees, then flying clear over a narrow ditch.
core.cn: 核心意象：屈膝蓄力，整个人腾空越过一道窄沟。

branches.en: a deer lifting off the bank
branches.cn: 从河岸跃起的鹿

branches.en: a runner clearing a low fence
branches.cn: 越过矮栅栏的跑者

branches.en: a line on a graph bending upward
branches.cn: 图表上陡然上弯的线

branches.en: a single step up that changes the level
branches.cn: 改变水平的一级台阶

branches.en: the same push, one over a fence and one over last year's figure
branches.cn: 同一次发力，一次越过栅栏，一次越过去年的数字

intro.en: An Old English verb, two past endings, and a compound with frog carry the family.
intro.cn: 一个古英语动词、两种过去式词尾，以及与 frog 的复合词支撑这个词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 租约；租期；出租；承租
definition_en: a legal contract by which someone rents property; the period of such a contract; to rent something out or to take it on rent
core_image: 一沓写满条款的合同，钥匙放在最后一页上
scene: 搬进公寓之前，两个人坐在桌前逐条看合同，最后在末尾签下名字。They signed a lease for the flat before the end of the month.
sceneCN: 这里是「租约」（第 1 个义项：租赁合同）；句意是他们在月底之前为公寓签了租约。图中可辨识物件：合同、签字笔、钥匙。

derivatives.zh: 由 lease 与 hold 复合而成，义为「租赁权；租赁地产」
由 leasehold 加 -er 构成，义为「承租人；租赁权持有人」
由 lease 加 -ing 构成，义为「租赁；租赁业务」

senses.title: A legal contract for renting property
senses.definition: a legal agreement under which one party rents property from another for a period
senses.definitionCN: 一方在某一期限内向另一方租用财产的法定协议
senses.example: They signed a lease for the flat before the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在月底之前为公寓签了租约。
senses.why: The French source named a letting of property, so the contract is the central sense from which the others grow.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源指财产的出租，所以契约是中心义项，其他义项都由它长出。

senses.title: The period covered by a contract
senses.definition: the length of time for which such a contract runs
senses.definitionCN: 这种合同持续的时长
senses.example: The lease runs for three years and can be renewed.
senses.exampleCN: 租期三年，可以续签。
senses.why: A contract always fixes a stretch of time, so the document's name easily transfers to the years it covers.
senses.whyCN: 合同总会确定一段时间，所以文书的名字很容易转指它所覆盖的那些年。

senses.title: To rent property out to someone
senses.definition: to let someone use property in return for rent
senses.definitionCN: 收取租金，让别人使用自己的财产
senses.example: The family leases the upper floors to a small company.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把楼上几层出租给一家小公司。
senses.why: If a contract lets someone use property, the owner can be said to lease it out, so the noun's name becomes a verb of granting.
senses.whyCN: 既然合同允许他人使用财产，所有者就可以说把财产出租出去，名词的名字于是变成表示授予的动词。

senses.title: To take and use property under a lease
senses.definition: to take property on a lease and pay rent for it
senses.definitionCN: 按租约取得财产使用权并支付租金
senses.example: We leased a car for the summer instead of buying one.
senses.exampleCN: 我们夏天租了一辆车，而不是买一辆。
senses.why: The same verb works from the other side of the contract: the tenant leases the thing that the landlord leases out.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也能从合同的另一边使用：租客承租的东西，正是房东出租的东西。

intro.en: Lease goes back to a Latin verb meaning to loosen or let go; through French it became the legal word for letting property to another person.
intro.cn: lease 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「放松、放开」的动词；经法语变成把财产让与他人使用的法律词。

items.en: The Latin adjective laxus meant loose or slack, not tightly held.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 laxus 意为松的、不紧的。

items.en: The verb laxare meant to loosen, release or let go.
items.cn: 动词 laxare 意为放松、放开或让出。

items.en: Old French lais named a letting of property, and laissier meant to let or leave.
items.cn: 古法语 lais 指财产的出租，动词 laissier 意为让出、留下。

items.en: Middle English les or lease named the contract and the right to hold land for a term.
items.cn: 中古英语 les 或 lease 指契约，以及按期限持有土地的权利。

items.en: Modern English keeps lease as both the contract and the act of renting out or taking on rent.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 lease 作名词指契约，也作动词指出租或承租。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the legal family and one same-root relative; the near-meaning group collects words for renting.
note.cn: 形近组收法律词族和一个同根词；近义组收表示租赁的词。

entries.definition: The right to hold property under a lease for a fixed term.
entries.definitionCN: 按租约在固定期限内持有财产的权利。

entries.definition: A person who holds property under a lease.
entries.definitionCN: 按租约持有财产的承租人。

entries.definition: To set free or let go; it shares the Latin verb laxare behind lease.
entries.definitionCN: 释放、放开；与 lease 共用背后的拉丁语动词 laxare。

entries.definition: A strap for holding an animal; only the spelling is close, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 牵住动物的皮带；只是拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: Money paid regularly for the use of property, or to pay it.
entries.definitionCN: 为使用财产定期支付的费用，或支付这笔费用。

entries.definition: To pay to use something for a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 付钱在短时间内使用某物。

entries.definition: To rent a house or room out to someone, chiefly in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 把房屋或房间出租给他人，主要用于英式英语。

entries.definition: To hire a ship or aircraft for a special purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途租用船只或飞机。

normalIntro.en: A Latin verb of loosening becomes a legal noun; the family then adds holders and a near relative, release.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「松开」的拉丁语动词变成法律名词；词族又添上持有人，以及近亲 release。

normal.en: Lease goes back to Latin laxare, to loosen, and the legal sense grows from letting property out of one's own hold.
normal.cn: lease 可追溯到拉丁语 laxare「松开」，法律义从「把财产从自己手里放出去」生长而来。

normal.en: The contract and the period share one word because a lease always fixes how long the arrangement lasts.
normal.cn: 契约与期限共用一个词，因为租约总要确定安排持续多久。

normal.en: Lease out is the landlord's direction, while lease from is the tenant's; the same verb serves both sides.
normal.cn: lease out 是房东的方向，lease from 是租客的方向；同一个动词服务双方。

normal.en: Leasehold and leaseholder add hold and -er to show the right and the person who holds it.
normal.cn: leasehold 与 leaseholder 加上 hold 和 -er，表明权利和持有权利的人。

normal.en: A new lease of life is a figurative lease: life is handed back for another term.
normal.cn: a new lease of life 是比喻性的租约：生命被重新交还一段时间。

abstract.en: To lease is to trade ownership for time, which is why the word sits between property and clock.
abstract.cn: 出租是用所有权换时间，所以这个词夹在财产与时钟之间。

abstract.en: A lease turns trust into paper: the arrangement survives even when the people who made it forget it.
abstract.cn: 租约把信任变成纸面：即使立约的人忘了，安排仍然存在。

abstract.en: The idea of loosening stays inside lease: something is let go for a while, then expected back.
abstract.cn: 「松开」的意思仍留在 lease 里：某物被放开一段时间，然后预期被归还。

examples.en: They signed a lease for the flat before the end of the month.
examples.cn: 他们在月底之前为公寓签了租约。

examples.en: The lease runs for three years and can be renewed.
examples.cn: 租期三年，可以续签。

examples.en: We leased a car for the summer instead of buying one.
examples.cn: 我们夏天租了一辆车，而不是买一辆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哩事」——租房合同里写满了「哩事」；lease 是租约。

root: 拉丁语 laxare（放松、放开）经古法语 lais（出租）进入中古英语 les/lease；与 lax、release 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a contract that lets property be used for a term; the senses divide into the period, the landlord's act and the tenant's act.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是允许他人在一定期限内使用财产的契约；义项由此分为租期、房东的出租和租客的承租。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of contract pages with a key resting on the last one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一沓合同纸，钥匙放在最后一页上。

branches.en: two people signing at the foot of a long document
branches.cn: 两人在一份长文件末尾签字

branches.en: a calendar with three years marked off
branches.cn: 标出三年时间的日历

branches.en: a landlord handing over a set of keys
branches.cn: 房东交出一串钥匙

branches.en: a family driving a rented car for one season
branches.cn: 一家人租一辆车用一个季节

branches.en: keys passed across a table after the ink dries
branches.cn: 墨迹干了以后钥匙在桌上递过去

intro.en: A Latin verb of loosening supplies the core, and English compounds with hold and suffixes for person and activity extend it.
intro.cn: 一个表示「松开」的拉丁语动词提供核心，英语再用 hold 构成复合词，并用表示人物和活动的后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 皮革；皮革制品；皮制的
definition_en: material made from the skin of animals, articles made from it, or the material used before a noun
core_image: 一块鞣好的牛皮摊在木台上，边缘还留着刀痕
scene: 作坊里，匠人把一张厚皮按在木台上，用刀顺着边裁下。The smell of new leather filled the small workshop.
sceneCN: 这里是「皮革」（第 1 个义项：动物皮制成的材料）；句意为新皮革的气味充满这间小作坊。可辨识画面：木台、厚皮、裁皮刀。

derivatives.zh: 由 leather 加 -y 构成，义为「像皮革的；坚韧的」
由 leather 加 -ette（仿制品）构成，义为「人造革」
由 leather 加 -en（由……制成的）构成，义为「皮革制的」（古旧用法）
由 leather 与 back 复合，义为「棱皮龟」

senses.title: Material made from animal skin
senses.definition: material made by treating the skin of animals so that it is soft and strong
senses.definitionCN: 把动物皮处理得柔软结实之后得到的材料
senses.example: The bag is made of soft brown leather.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包用柔软的棕色皮革制成。
senses.why: Old English leþer named the treated hide itself, and that material sense has stayed the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 leþer 指处理过的兽皮本身，这层材料义一直是这个词的中心。

senses.title: Articles made of leather
senses.definition: things made from leather, especially when spoken of in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 用皮革制成的物品，尤指用复数形式时
senses.example: He cleaned his leathers after the ride.
senses.exampleCN: 骑完车后他清理了皮衣。
senses.why: Because a material can stand for the things cut from it, tanned skins become leathers in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 材料可以代替用它制成的东西，鞣好的皮在复数里就成了皮衣、皮具。

senses.title: Used before a noun to mean made of leather
senses.definition: placed before another noun to say that the thing is made of leather
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示该物由皮革制成
senses.example: She wore a leather jacket in the cold wind.
senses.exampleCN: 寒风里她穿着皮夹克。
senses.why: English often lets a material noun work as a modifier, so leather needs no suffix to describe a jacket.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让材料名词直接作修饰语，所以 leather 不加后缀就能修饰 jacket。

intro.en: An Old English noun for treated hide is the direct source, and its Germanic shape is still easy to hear.
intro.cn: 一个指处理过兽皮的古英语名词是直接来源，它的日耳曼语形态至今仍容易辨认。

items.en: Leþer named the skin of an animal after treatment, and it is the direct source of the word.
items.cn: leþer 指处理之后的兽皮，是这个词的直接来源。

items.en: The Germanic form behind it is reconstructed as leþra-, with related words in other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 其背后的日耳曼语形式被重构为 leþra-，在其他日耳曼语言里有相关词。

items.en: The old word may be related to the idea of a hide, though the exact link is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个旧词可能与「兽皮」的观念有关，但具体联系并不确定。

items.en: Middle English kept leather for the material and began using it for goods made of it.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 leather 指材料，并开始用它指由它制成的物品。

items.en: Modern English uses leather for the material, for leather goods, and as a word placed before nouns.
items.cn: 现代英语用 leather 指材料、指皮具，也把它放在名词前作修饰。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built from leather and words with a similar shape; the near-meaning group collects other words for skins and leather types.
note.cn: 形近组收由 leather 构成的形式以及形状相近的词；近义组收表示兽皮与皮革种类的其他用词。

entries.definition: Tough and dry like leather.
entries.definitionCN: 像皮革一样坚韧干燥。

entries.definition: A manufactured material made to look like leather.
entries.definitionCN: 做成皮革样子的人造材料。

entries.definition: The state of the air outside, sun, rain or wind.
entries.definitionCN: 户外空气的状态，晴、雨或风；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: One of the light growths covering a bird.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖鸟类身体的轻软生成物之一。

entries.definition: The skin of a large animal, raw or tanned.
entries.definitionCN: 大型动物的皮，生的或鞣过的。

entries.definition: The outer covering of a body, or material from it.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的外层覆盖物，或由此得来的材料。

entries.definition: Leather with a soft brushed surface.
entries.definitionCN: 表面经过打磨起绒的软革。

entries.definition: The soft hair covering an animal, or a coat made of it.
entries.definitionCN: 动物身上的软毛，或由此制成的衣物。

normalIntro.en: A noun of treated hide and four English endings that build qualities, imitations and compounds hold this word together.
normalIntro.cn: 一个指处理过兽皮的名词，与四个造出性质、仿制品及复合词的英语词尾，共同支撑着这个词。

normal.en: Old English leþer is the direct source, and the th sound in the middle has never changed.
normal.cn: 古英语 leþer 是直接来源，中间那个 th 音一直没变。

normal.en: Leathery adds -y: having the toughness and dryness of leather.
normal.cn: leathery 加 -y，意为具有皮革的坚韧与干燥。

normal.en: Leatherette adds -ette, a suffix for imitations, so it is leather that is not leather.
normal.cn: leatherette 加 -ette，这是表示仿制品的后缀，所以是「不是皮革的皮革」。

normal.en: Leatherback is leather plus back, naming a turtle with a tough shell instead of hard plates.
normal.cn: leatherback 是 leather 加 back，指背甲坚韧而非硬板的龟。

normal.en: In a leather jacket, leather works as a modifier without any suffix.
normal.cn: 在 a leather jacket 里，leather 不加后缀就作修饰语。

abstract.en: A material word can name the goods made from it, so leathers means leather clothes.
abstract.cn: 材料词可以指用它做成的东西，所以 leathers 指皮衣。

abstract.en: Toughness is the memory of a hide that had to protect an animal, carried into a jacket.
abstract.cn: 坚韧是兽皮曾保护过动物的记忆，被带进了一件夹克。

abstract.en: English rarely marks material with a suffix, so leather sits before a noun and quietly becomes an adjective.
abstract.cn: 英语很少用后缀标记材料，于是 leather 直接站在名词前，悄悄变成形容词。

examples.en: The bag is made of soft brown leather.
examples.cn: 这个包用柔软的棕色皮革制成。

examples.en: She wore a leather jacket in the cold wind.
examples.cn: 寒风里她穿着皮夹克。

examples.en: He cleaned his leathers after the ride.
examples.cn: 骑完车后他清理了皮衣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累着」——皮衣厚重，穿着走一天累着了；记住 leather 是皮革。

root: 古英语 leþer（处理过的兽皮），与日耳曼语中重构的 leþra- 同源；与拉丁语 corium 无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is treated animal skin; the senses then add the plural goods made from it and its use as a word before nouns.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是处理过的兽皮；义项由此加上用复数表示的皮具，以及放在名词前作修饰的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tanned hide spread on a wooden bench, a knife at its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：木台上摊开的鞣制兽皮，边缘搁着裁皮刀。

branches.en: a hide being worked with a knife on a bench
branches.cn: 木台上被刀修整的兽皮

branches.en: a row of leather jackets hanging in a shop
branches.cn: 店里挂着的一排皮衣

branches.en: a jacket described by the material it is cut from
branches.cn: 用其材料来描述的夹克

branches.en: a wallet softened by years in a pocket
branches.cn: 在口袋里磨软的钱包

branches.en: a belt with a worn buckle, still strong
branches.cn: 扣子磨旧却仍结实的皮带

intro.en: An Old English noun of treated hide and four English endings that build qualities, imitations and compounds.
intro.cn: 一个指处理过兽皮的古英语名词，以及四个造出性质、仿制品与复合词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; Latin corium, a different word for hide, is not its source.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语；拉丁语 corium 是另一个表示兽皮的词，并非它的来源。

items.meaning: leather plus back, a kind of turtle

definition_zh: 讲座；授课；（大学的）课时；讲稿；训斥
definition_en: a formal talk given to teach or inform, a course session built on such talks, the written text of a talk, a serious scolding, or, in older use, the act of reading
core_image: 讲台前的一束光：把文字拣出来，念给台下的人听
scene: 大学阶梯教室里，教授把讲义摊在讲台上。He began a lecture on the history of the city, and the students below wrote so fast that their pens never stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 lecture 是「讲座、课堂讲授」（第 2 个义项：面向听众的正式讲授）；句意：他开始一场关于城市史的讲座，下面学生的笔一直没停。图中可辨识物件：阶梯教室、讲台、摊开的讲义、投影幕、学生的笔记本。

senses.title: Reading aloud: the act of reading
senses.definition: the act of reading a text, especially aloud and in a formal setting (now archaic)
senses.definitionCN: 阅读文本的行为，尤指在正式场合朗读（现已古旧）
senses.example: In the monastery the lecture of the psalm began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院里，晨祷时对圣咏的诵读从黎明开始。
senses.why: Lecture came from Medieval Latin lectura, 'a reading'. Before it named a talk, it named the act of reading itself, and the oldest English examples keep that plain sense.
senses.whyCN: lecture 来自中世纪拉丁语 lectura“阅读”。在它指“讲座”之前，它指的就是“读”这个行为，最早的英语用例保留着这层朴素含义。

senses.title: A formal talk that teaches
senses.titleCN: 讲座：面向听众的正式讲授
senses.definition: a formal talk given to a group of people, especially students, in order to teach or inform them
senses.definitionCN: 为教授或告知一群人（尤指学生）而作的正式讲话
senses.example: She went to a lecture on the history of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她去听了一场关于这座城市历史的讲座。
senses.why: In the 16c a lecture was a discourse read or delivered before an audience. The act of reading aloud turned into the public teaching talk, which is now the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 在 16 世纪，lecture 指向听众读出或讲出的一段论述。“朗读”这个动作由此变成公开的教学讲话，也就是今天最核心的义项。

senses.title: A course unit: one class in a series
senses.titleCN: 课时：课程中的一个讲授单元
senses.definition: a single period of instruction in a course, or the course seen as a series of such talks
senses.definitionCN: 课程中的一节讲授，或由一系列讲授构成的整门课
senses.example: The course consists of twelve lectures and four seminars.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课由十二次讲授和四次研讨课组成。
senses.why: Once a lecture is put on a timetable, the talk becomes the unit of a course. Attendance is counted in lectures, and the syllabus is divided into them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦讲座被排进课表，这场讲话就成了课程的计量单位。出勤按“讲”计算，教学大纲也按讲次划分。

senses.title: The written text of a talk
senses.titleCN: 讲稿：写在纸上的那份讲授
senses.definition: the written text or full notes from which a talk is delivered, or a published version of it
senses.definitionCN: 演讲所依据的书面文本或完整讲稿，也指其出版形式
senses.example: She wrote out the lecture in full before rehearsing it.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把讲稿完整写出来，再开始排练。
senses.why: A talk can be fixed on paper before or after it is spoken. The same noun then names the script the speaker holds, which is why one can write, revise or print a lecture.
senses.whyCN: 讲话在说之前或之后都可以固定在纸上。同一个名词于是也指讲者手里的稿子，所以说“写讲稿、改讲稿、印讲稿”都成立。

senses.title: A serious scolding
senses.definition: a long, serious talk to someone about their behaviour, given as a warning or punishment
senses.definitionCN: 就某人的行为作长时间严肃谈话，作为警告或惩罚
senses.example: His father gave him a lecture about wasting money.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲就乱花钱的事训了他一顿。
senses.why: The instructive frame is now aimed at correction. The content is still teaching, but the listener is being told off, so praise and warning replace neutral explanation.
senses.whyCN: 讲授的框架这时对准了“纠正”：内容仍是在教，但听者是在挨批评，于是中性的讲解换成了告诫与责难。

senses.title: Verb: teach by giving talks
senses.definition: to give a formal talk to students or to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 给学生或听众作正式讲授
senses.example: Professor Lin lectures on constitutional history.
senses.exampleCN: 林教授讲授宪政史。
senses.why: This is zero derivation: the noun became a verb with no added suffix, naming the activity of the person behind the lectern.
senses.whyCN: 这是零派生：名词不加任何后缀直接变成动词，指讲台后面那个人所做的事。

senses.title: Verb: scold at length
senses.definition: to talk seriously and at length to someone about something they have done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 就某人做错的事进行长时间严肃谈话
senses.example: The coach lectured the team for giving up in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 教练因球队下半场放弃而训了他们一顿。
senses.why: The verb takes the corrective branch too. Now it has a target and a fault, and the length of the talk is part of the reproach.
senses.whyCN: 动词也接上了“纠正”这一支：此时它带有对象和过错，而“讲得很长”本身就是责难的一部分。

senses.title: A public lecture as an event
senses.titleCN: 公开讲座：作为活动的讲演
senses.definition: a public talk organized as an event, often by a university, museum or learned society
senses.definitionCN: 作为活动组织的公开演讲，常由大学、博物馆或学术团体举办
senses.example: The museum's annual lecture drew an audience of five hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的年度讲座吸引了五百名听众。
senses.why: The form spreads beyond the classroom. A lecture can now be an event with a title, a guest speaker and tickets, even when no course is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这种形式走出了课堂。lecture 现在可以是一场有标题、有嘉宾讲者、需要门票的活动，即使并不附属于任何课程。

intro.en: Lecture is a reading word before it is a teaching word. Latin legere 'to read' goes back to 'pick out, gather', and English first used lecture for the act of reading, then for the talk.
intro.cn: lecture 先是“阅读”词，后来才是“教学”词。拉丁语 legere“读”的本义是“拣出、采集”；英语先用它指阅读行为，再指讲授。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'the act of reading, a reading aloud', borrowed from Medieval Latin lectura.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期的英语，意为“阅读行为、朗读”，借自中世纪拉丁语 lectura。

items.en: lectura 'a reading' is a noun of action from lectus, the past participle of legere 'to read'.
items.cn: lectura“阅读”是由 legere“读”的过去分词 lectus 构成的行为名词。

items.en: legere meant 'to read', but its older sense was 'to pick out, select, gather'. Reading is pictured as picking out letters one by one from the page.
items.cn: legere 意为“读”，更早的意思是“拣出、挑选、采集”。阅读被想象成从页面上把字母一个个拣出来。

items.en: legere is traced to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather, pick out'. The step from 'gather' to 'read' is inferred rather than attested, so this deeper link is generally accepted.
items.cn: legere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“收集、采集、拣出”。从“采集”到“读”这一步是推论而非有据可查，因此这层更深的联系属于一般认为是。

items.en: The sense 'a discourse read or delivered before an audience' appears in the 16c. By the 17c lecture is the ordinary word for a university talk, and the old 'reading' sense fades.
items.cn: “向听众读出或讲出的一段论述”这一义项见于 16 世纪。到 17 世纪，lecture 已是大学讲课的常用词，旧的“阅读”义逐渐退场。

items.en: Lecture and legal are not the same family: legere is the verb 'to read', while lex (genitive legis) is the noun 'law'. Both contain the leg- shape and are traced to *leg- 'gather', but law is not a form of 'read'.
items.cn: lecture 与 legal 并非同一家族：legere 是动词“读”，lex（属格 legis）是名词“法”。两者都含 leg- 这一形，都被追溯到 *leg-“采集”，但“法”并不是“读”的某种形式。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the reading root legere from the law noun lex. The near-meaning group separates a teaching talk from other kinds of public speech.
note.cn: 形近组把“读”的词根 legere 与“法”的名词 lex 分开；近义组把教学性讲授与其他类型的公开讲话分开。

entries.definition: a stand for a book or notes, used by someone who is reading or speaking. It comes from the same legere 'read' family, not from lecture itself.
entries.definitionCN: 供朗读或演讲者放置书本、讲稿的架子。它出自同一个 legere“读”的词族，而不是由 lecture 派生。

entries.definition: clear enough to be read. It is legere plus -ibilis 'able to be', so it describes writing that can be read, not a talk that is given.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚、可辨认的。它是 legere 加 -ibilis“能够被……”，形容文字可读，而不是形容所作的讲座。

entries.definition: the body that makes laws. It looks as if it contains lecture's root, but it is lex 'law' plus lator 'proposer', so the meaning is law-making, not reading.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关。它看起来含有 lecture 的词根，其实是 lex“法”加 lator“提出者”，所以意思是立法，而不是阅读。

entries.definition: a formal address to an audience. It is broader than lecture and need not teach anything; a lecture is expected to inform.
entries.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话。它比 lecture 宽泛，不必包含教学；而 lecture 默认要传递知识。

entries.definition: a class in which a small group discusses a topic. It is interactive and smaller, while a lecture is one voice addressing many.
entries.definitionCN: 小组讨论某个主题的课程。它强调互动且人数少，而 lecture 是一个声音对许多人讲。

entries.definition: a talk on a religious or moral theme, usually delivered in worship. It aims at the conscience, not at course content.
entries.definitionCN: 关于宗教或道德主题的讲话，通常在礼拜中宣讲。它对准的是良知，而不是课程内容。

entries.definition: a formal or official rebuke. It is usually shorter and more procedural than a lecture, which explains and moralizes at length.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或官方的斥责。它通常比 lecture 短、更讲程序，而 lecture 会长篇解释并说教。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: legere 'read', its past participle lectus, and the English family lectern, legible, legend and lesson.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：legere“读”、它的过去分词 lectus，以及英语中的 lectern、legible、legend、lesson。

normal.en: legere 'to read' gives the lect- stem; lecture is literally 'a reading' before it is a talk.
normal.cn: legere“读”给出 lect- 这个词干；lecture 字面上就是“一次阅读”，之后才成为“讲座”。

normal.en: lectern, legible, legend and lesson all come from the same 'read / pick out' family, so the reading image is still visible around lecture.
normal.cn: lectern、legible、legend、lesson 都出自同一个“读／拣出”词族，因此“阅读”的意象在 lecture 周围仍然看得见。

normal.en: The old sense 'a reading' explains why a lecture was once something read aloud rather than freely spoken.
normal.cn: 古义“一次阅读”解释了为什么 lecture 早先是“朗读出来的东西”，而不是即兴讲话。

normal.en: lecture notes and lecture hall keep the classroom frame: notes record the talk, the hall houses it.
normal.cn: lecture notes 与 lecture hall 保留着课堂框架：笔记记录讲授，讲堂容纳讲授。

normal.en: give somebody a lecture moves the same talk from teaching to correcting, which is why the verb can mean 'scold'.
normal.cn: give somebody a lecture 把同一场讲话从“教”移到“纠正”，所以动词可以表示“训斥”。

abstract.en: Picture a page under a lamp: letters are picked out one by one, then the same words are spoken to rows of listeners. Lecture is that page becoming a voice.
abstract.cn: 想象台灯下的一页纸：字母被一个个拣出来，随后同一串词被念给一排排听众。lecture 就是那页纸变成声音的过程。

abstract.en: The voice can teach or scold; only the listener's posture changes — a notebook open, or a head held down.
abstract.cn: 同一个声音可以教人，也可以训人；变的只是听者的姿态——要么摊开笔记本，要么低着头。

abstract.en: A lecture is a text that has learned to stand up and speak, and a course is a row of such texts standing in line.
abstract.cn: 一场 lecture 是一段学会站起来说话的文字，而一门课程就是这样的文字排成一列。

examples.en: The lecture on volcanoes was full of photographs from the 1980 eruption.
examples.cn: 那场关于火山的讲座满是 1980 年喷发的照片。

examples.en: He lectures to first-year students three mornings a week.
examples.cn: 他每周有三个上午给一年级学生授课。

examples.en: My mother lectured me for twenty minutes about the unpaid bill.
examples.cn: 母亲为那张没付的账单训了我二十分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: “来课扯”——上课时把内容扯成一大段 → lecture 讲座、训斥

root: 拉丁语 legere“读”（本义“采集、挑选”）→ 中世纪拉丁 lectura“阅读”，核心是“把文字拣出来、念给人听”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of lecture, one movement: a text is picked out and read, the reading becomes a talk, the talk becomes a course unit and a script, and finally the same instructive voice turns into a scolding.
sensesIntro.cn: lecture 的八个义项是一条运动线：文字被拣出来读，读变成讲授，讲授变成课时与讲稿，最后同一种“教导口吻”变成训斥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words are picked out of a page and spoken to people who came to listen.
core.cn: 核心意象：把字从纸页上拣出来，念给前来听的人。

branches.en: READING: the oldest layer, when lecture names the act of reading rather than a talk.
branches.cn: 阅读：最古老的一层，此时 lecture 指的是“读”这一行为，而不是讲座。

branches.en: INSTRUCTION: the classroom talk, the verb for giving it, and the public lecture as an event.
branches.cn: 讲授：课堂讲座、表示“讲授”的动词，以及作为活动的公开讲座。

branches.en: COURSE UNIT: the talk becomes a countable slot in a timetable and a syllabus.
branches.cn: 课时：讲座变成课表与教学大纲里可计数的一格。

branches.en: WRITTEN TEXT: the spoken words are fixed on paper as a script or a printed talk.
branches.cn: 书面文本：说出的话被固定在纸上，成为讲稿或印行的讲辞。

branches.en: CORRECTION: the instructive voice turns into a long scolding, as a noun and as a verb.
branches.cn: 纠正：教导的口吻变成长篇训斥，名词与动词都走这一支。

intro.en: Lecture is a borrowed Latin noun, not a prefixed English word. English adds only ordinary suffixes: -er for the person, -ship for the post, -ing for the activity; the noun also became a verb with no suffix at all.
intro.cn: lecture 是借入的拉丁名词，不是由英语前缀构成的词。英语只加普通后缀：-er 表人，-ship 表职位，-ing 表活动；名词还零派生成了动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base legere 'read / pick out' has a large family. Note that lex 'law' is a different noun with a similar shape, and legare 'send, bequeath' is a different verb again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 legere“读／拣出”有一个很大的词族。注意 lex“法”是形似的另一个名词，legare“派出、遗赠”又是另一个动词。

items.meaning: a person who gives lectures, especially at a university
items.meaningCN: 讲师；授课者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The lecturer paused to answer a question.
items.exampleCN: 讲师停下来回答了一个问题。

items.meaning: the post or position of a lecturer
items.meaningCN: 讲师职位；讲席（-ship 表示职位或身份）
items.example: She was appointed to a lectureship in physics.
items.exampleCN: 她获聘物理学讲师职位。

items.meaningCN: 授课；讲学（-ing 构成行为名词）
items.example: His lecturing took him to six countries.
items.exampleCN: 他的讲学让他去了六个国家。

items.meaning: to give a lecture; to scold at length
items.meaningCN: 讲授；长篇训斥（名动同形，不加后缀）

items.meaning: to read; to pick out, gather
items.example: The verb is the root shared by lecture, lector and collect.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 lecture、lector、collect 共有的词根。

items.example: Every English word on this stem keeps the reading image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干上的英语词都保留“读”的意象。

items.example: It turns the act of reading into the noun lecture.
items.exampleCN: 它把“读”的动作变成名词 lecture。

items.meaning: a reader; one who reads aloud in a service
items.meaningCN: 诵读者；（礼拜中的）读经员
items.example: The lector read the passage aloud to the congregation.
items.exampleCN: 读经员向会众朗读了那段经文。

items.structure: Medieval Latin lectrum, from the stem lect-
items.meaning: a reading desk, especially in a church
items.example: She set her notes on the lectern before speaking.
items.exampleCN: 发言前她把讲稿放在讲台上。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be read; clear enough to read
latinEntries.meaningCN: 可读的；字迹清晰的（-ibilis 表“能够被……”）

latinEntries.meaning: a story handed down; originally 'things to be read' about the saints
latinEntries.meaningCN: 传说；原指关于圣徒“应被诵读的事迹”

latinEntries.meaning: a unit of teaching; originally a passage read aloud

latinEntries.meaning: to bring things together; literally 'to gather up'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 收集；字面义“把东西拣到一起”

definition_en: relating to law, allowed or required by law, valid in law, connected with the legal profession, or allowed by the rules of a game
core_image: 一部摊开的法典，页边压着印章：允许什么、要求什么，都写在上面
scene: 律所的会议室里，律师把合同翻到签字页。She pointed out that the clause was not legal in this country and had to be rewritten before anyone could sign.

（美）法定尺寸纸张；法律文件（常用复数 legals）

collocations.zh: 黄色横线稿纸（法定尺寸）

senses.title: Relating to law in general
senses.definition: connected with the law, the courts, or the system of rules a society enforces
senses.definitionCN: 与法律、法院或社会所执行的规则体系有关的
senses.example: She is studying the legal systems of two countries.
senses.exampleCN: 她在研究两个国家的法律体系。
senses.why: Legal began as the adjective of Latin lex 'law', so its widest sense simply marks anything belonging to the law as an institution.
senses.whyCN: legal 最初是拉丁语 lex“法”的形容词，因此最宽的义项只是标记“属于法律这个制度”的事物。

senses.title: Allowed by law
senses.definition: permitted by law; not forbidden or criminal
senses.definitionCN: 为法律所允许的；未被禁止或不算犯罪的
senses.example: In some states it is legal to record a call you take part in.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些州，录下自己参与的通话是合法的。
senses.why: From 'belonging to law' comes 'consistent with law'. The question is no longer what law is about, but whether an act falls inside the permitted line.
senses.whyCN: 从“属于法律”引申出“符合法律”。问题不再是“法管什么”，而是一个行为是否落在被允许的界线之内。

senses.title: Required by law
senses.definition: required or prescribed by law, so that not doing it is a breach
senses.definitionCN: 由法律要求或规定的，不做即构成违法或违约
senses.example: Employers have a legal duty to provide safety training.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主有提供安全培训的法定义务。
senses.why: The same boundary has a second side: what law permits it also commands. A legal duty is not optional, and the adjective shifts from permission to obligation.
senses.whyCN: 同一条界线还有另一面：法律允许的东西，也可以被法律命令。legal duty 不是可选项，形容词于是从“许可”滑向“义务”。

senses.title: Valid and enforceable in law
senses.definition: recognized as valid and enforceable by law, especially of a document, contract or claim
senses.definitionCN: 被法律认可为有效且可执行的，尤指文件、合同或主张
senses.example: The contract is not legal without both signatures.
senses.exampleCN: 没有双方签字，这份合同在法律上不生效。
senses.why: Here legal does not mean 'allowed' but 'having legal force'. A document can be legally made yet legally ineffective if a formality is missing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 legal 不是“被允许”，而是“具有法律效力”。一份文件可以依法制作，却因缺少形式要件而在法律上无效。

senses.title: Of the legal profession
senses.definition: relating to lawyers, their training, or the business of giving legal advice
senses.definitionCN: 与律师、其训练或提供法律意见的业务有关的
senses.example: He left banking for a legal career at thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十岁时离开银行业，转做法律职业。
senses.why: The institution is also a trade. Legal then describes the people and practices that operate the system, not the rules themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律这套制度同时也是一门行业。legal 于是描述运作这套制度的人与业务，而不是规则本身。

senses.title: Relating to lawsuits
senses.definition: relating to court proceedings or to action taken through the courts
senses.definitionCN: 与法院程序或通过法院采取的行动有关的
senses.example: The tenants threatened legal action over the mould.
senses.exampleCN: 租户因霉斑问题威胁要采取法律诉讼。
senses.why: One branch of the system is dispute. Legal action names the step from a private quarrel to a case that a court can decide.
senses.whyCN: 这套制度的一支是争端。legal action 标记了从私人纠纷跨到“法院可以裁决的案件”的那一步。

senses.title: According to the letter of the law
senses.definition: existing or holding a status in law, even if the actual situation is different
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上存在或拥有某种身份，即使实际情况不同
senses.example: She is the legal owner, though her brother runs the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 她是法律上的所有者，尽管农场由她哥哥经营。
senses.why: Law can assign a name that reality does not match. Legal owner, legal parent and legal fiction all use the adjective to mark the official version, as opposed to the factual one.
senses.whyCN: 法律可以给出一个与现实不符的名义。legal owner、legal parent、legal fiction 都用这个形容词标记“官方版本”，以区别于事实版本。

senses.title: Allowed by the rules of a game
senses.definition: allowed by the rules of a sport or game, though not necessarily by statute
senses.definitionCN: 为运动或游戏规则所允许的，而不一定涉及成文法
senses.example: The tackle was hard but legal.
senses.exampleCN: 那次擒抱很凶，但符合规则。
senses.why: The boundary image is borrowed from law: a game has its own code, and a move inside it is called legal by analogy. Here no court is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这里借用了“界线”的意象：游戏有自己的规则法典，规则内的动作被类比地称为 legal，此时并不涉及法院。

senses.title: Legal-size paper
senses.definition: a US paper size of 8.5 by 14 inches, sold as legal pads and used for long documents
senses.definitionCN: 美国一种 8.5×14 英寸的纸张规格，做成黄色横线稿纸，用于较长的文书
senses.example: He drafted the will on a yellow legal pad.
senses.exampleCN: 他在黄色法定尺寸稿纸上起草了遗嘱。
senses.why: The adjective became a fixed label for a paper size once associated with legal records. This is an attributive use, not a new legal concept.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词固定成了纸张规格的标签，因为这种尺寸曾与法律文书相关。这是定语用法，并不是新的法律概念。

intro.en: Legal is a direct Latin borrowing, not a French one: English took legalis from Latin in the 15c, while loyal came through French from the same source. Its noun is lex, not legare and not licere.
intro.cn: legal 是直接借自拉丁语，而非借自法语：英语在 15 世纪直接取用 legalis；loyal 则是同一来源经法语变来的。它的名词是 lex，不是 legare，也不是 licere。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'of or pertaining to law'. It was borrowed straight from Latin legalis rather than through French.
items.cn: 最早记录于 15 世纪中期的英语，意为“与法律有关的”。它是直接从拉丁语 legalis 借入的，而不是经法语转手。

items.en: legalis 'of or belonging to the law' is formed from lex (genitive legis) 'law, statute, bill' plus -alis 'relating to'.
items.cn: legalis“属于法律的”由 lex（属格 legis）“法、法规、议案”加 -alis“与……有关的”构成。

items.en: lex is traced to PIE *leg- 'to collect, gather'. The idea may be 'that which is collected or laid down', but this semantic step is generally accepted, not documented.
items.cn: lex 被追溯到原始印欧语 *leg-“收集、采集”。其理据可能是“被收集、被放下之物”，但这一步只是一般认为是，并无文献确证。

items.en: legare 'to send, depute; bequeath' is a different verb, source of legate, legacy and allegation. Its connection with lex is source uncertain, so legal must not be treated as derived from legare.
items.cn: legare“派出、委任；遗赠”是另一个动词，是 legate、legacy、allegation 的来源。它与 lex 的联系来源不确定，因此不能把 legal 当作 legare 的派生词。

items.en: licere 'to be permitted' is a third root, the source of license. Being permitted by someone is not the same as being lawful under a statute.
items.cn: licere“被允许”是第三条词根线，是 license 的来源。被某人允许，与在成文法下合法，并不是同一件事。

items.en: Legal now covers the system, permission, obligation, validity and the profession. Loyal, legate and legacy are close relatives in form but come by different routes, so their meanings must not be merged.
items.cn: 现代 legal 覆盖法律体系、许可、义务、效力和法律职业。loyal、legate、legacy 在形式上亲近，却走了不同路线，词义不可合并。

note.en: The look-alike group mixes three neighbours: one from legere 'read', one genuinely from lex, and one from legare 'bequeath'. The near-meaning group separates permission, justification, statute and the courts.
note.cn: 形近组混入三个邻居：一个出自 legere“读”，一个确实出自 lex，一个出自 legare“遗赠”。近义组则把许可、正当性、成文法与法院区分开。

entries.definition: clear enough to read. It looks like legal but comes from legere 'to read', so it has nothing to do with law.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚可读的。它形似 legal，却出自 legere“读”，与法律无关。

entries.definition: lawful or valid; also reasonable and justified. It comes from Latin legitimus, built on lex, so it is a true cousin of legal.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的、有效的；也指合情合理的。它来自以 lex 构成的拉丁语 legitimus，是 legal 真正的同族词。

entries.definition: money or property left to someone by a will. It looks legal, but it comes from legare 'bequeath', not from lex 'law'.
entries.definitionCN: 遗嘱留给某人的钱财或财产。它形似 legal，却出自 legare“遗赠”，而非 lex“法”。

entries.definition: allowed by law; not against the law. It is plainer and older than legal and often carries a moral tone that legal lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 法律允许的；不违法的。它比 legal 更朴素、更古老，常带有 legal 所缺的道德意味。

entries.definition: valid according to law or reason. Unlike legal, it can also mean 'fair and justified' outside any statute.
entries.definitionCN: 依法律或依理性有效的。与 legal 不同，它还可以指任何法规之外的事情“合理、正当”。

entries.definition: required or created by a written statute. It is narrower and more technical than legal, which covers the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 由成文法规定或创设的。它比 legal 更窄、更技术化，因为 legal 覆盖整个法律体系。

entries.definition: relating to courts, judges, or the administration of justice. It names one branch of the system, not law as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与法院、法官或司法有关的。它指体系中的一个分支，而不是整个法律。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: lex (genitive legis) 'law' + -alis, with legitimate, legislature and loyal in the same family. Watch the false friends legere 'read' and legare 'bequeath'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：lex（属格 legis）“法”+ -alis，同族有 legitimate、legislature、loyal。要警惕形近假朋友 legere“读”与 legare“遗赠”。

normal.en: lex, legis is the noun 'law'; legalis adds -alis 'relating to'. The core is simply 'of the law'.
normal.cn: lex、legis 是名词“法”；legalis 加上 -alis“与……有关”。核心意思就是“属于法的”。

normal.en: legitimate and legislature are built on the same lex, which is why they all carry a law meaning.
normal.cn: legitimate 与 legislature 都建在同一个 lex 上，所以它们都带“法”的含义。

normal.en: legacy comes from legare 'bequeath', not from lex. A legacy is what a will leaves, not what a statute says.
normal.cn: legacy 出自 legare“遗赠”，不是 lex。legacy 是遗嘱留下的东西，不是法规规定的条文。

normal.en: loyal is legalis after its trip through French: same source, different word. Loyalty is faithfulness, not legality.
normal.cn: loyal 是 legalis 经法语旅行后的样子：同源而异词。loyalty 是忠诚，不是合法性。

normal.en: legal age and legal duty show the two sides of the boundary: one permits, the other obliges.
normal.cn: legal age 与 legal duty 展示同一条界线的两面：一面是允许，一面是强制。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn on a floor: inside it, everything is allowed; on the line, everything is required; outside it, nothing is recognized. Legal is the line itself, seen from any side.
abstract.cn: 想象地板上画的一条线：线内一切被允许，线上一切被要求，线外一切不被承认。legal 就是这条线本身，从哪一面看都算。

abstract.en: The same stamp can mean 'you may', 'you must' or 'this counts', depending on which document it lands on.
abstract.cn: 同一枚印章落在不同文件上，可以表示“你可以”“你必须”或“这份算数”。

abstract.en: Law has a name for things that do not exist in fact: the legal owner is a person the paper sees, not always the person the field sees.
abstract.cn: 法律会为事实上不存在的东西命名：法律上的所有者是纸面看见的人，未必是田里看见的人。

examples.en: The company sought legal advice before signing the deal.
examples.cn: 公司在签署交易前寻求法律咨询。

examples.en: Is it legal to park here after six?
examples.cn: 六点以后在这里停车合法吗？

examples.en: She was the legal owner of the flat but had never lived in it.
examples.cn: 她是这套公寓法律上的所有者，却从未住过。

dict_mnemonic.text: “李哥”——李哥办事只走正规手续 → legal 合法的、法律的

root: 拉丁语 lex（属格 legis）“法”+ -alis“与……有关的”，核心是“写在法典里、有法律依据”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of legal, all radiating from one noun, lex. A thing can belong to the law, be allowed by it, be required by it, be valid under it, be done by its professionals, or merely carry its label.
sensesIntro.cn: legal 的九个义项都从一个名词 lex 放射出来：某事物可以属于法律、被法律允许、被法律要求、在法律上有效、由法律从业者去做，或只是贴着法律的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line written into a code, marking what is allowed, required and recognized.
core.cn: 核心意象：写进法典的一条界线，标出什么被允许、什么被要求、什么被承认。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND PROFESSION: law as an institution, and the people who operate it.
branches.cn: 体系与职业：作为制度的法律，以及运作它的人。

branches.en: PERMISSION: what statute allows, and, by analogy, what the rules of a game allow.
branches.cn: 许可：成文法允许的事，以及类比到游戏规则所允许的事。

branches.en: OBLIGATION: the other side of the boundary, where the law commands rather than permits.
branches.cn: 义务：界线的另一面，法律在这里不是允许而是命令。

branches.en: LEGAL EFFECT: validity, court action, and the official status that may differ from fact.
branches.cn: 法律效力：有效性、诉讼，以及可能与事实不同的官方身份。

branches.en: PAPER SIZE: a fixed attributive use, where the adjective labels a format rather than a legal idea.
branches.cn: 纸张规格：固定的定语用法，形容词在这里标记的是尺寸，而不是法律概念。

intro.en: Legal is a Latin adjective borrowed whole. English adds -ly for the adverb, -ity for the abstract noun, -ize for the verb, and the negative prefix il- before l.
intro.cn: legal 是整体借入的拉丁形容词。英语加 -ly 构成副词，-ity 构成抽象名词，-ize 构成动词，并在 l 前用否定前缀 il-。

latinIntro.en: The lex family is wide: legitimate, legislature, loyal and privilege all contain the law noun in different shapes. Keep it apart from legere 'read' and legare 'bequeath'.
latinIntro.cn: lex 词族很宽：legitimate、legislature、loyal、privilege 都以不同形态含有“法”这个名词。要把它与 legere“读”、legare“遗赠”分开。

items.meaning: in a way that is allowed by law; according to law
items.meaningCN: 合法地；在法律上（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 那场抗议是合法举行的。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being legal
items.meaningCN: 合法性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: The court questioned the legality of the search.
items.exampleCN: 法院质疑那次搜查的合法性。

items.meaning: to make something legal by law
items.example: Several states have legalized recreational use.
items.exampleCN: 有几个州已将娱乐性使用合法化。

items.meaningCN: 非法的；违法的（il- 是否定前缀，用在 l 前）
items.example: It is illegal to dump waste in the river.
items.exampleCN: 向河里倾倒废物是违法的。

items.example: The noun supplies the law at the centre of legal.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供 legal 核心的“法”。

items.example: The stem appears in legal, legislate and legitimate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 legal、legislate 与 legitimate。

items.example: It turns the noun for law into the adjective legal.
items.exampleCN: 它把“法”这个名词变成形容词 legal。

items.meaning: the quality or state of being
items.example: It forms legality, the quality of being lawful.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 legality，即合乎法律的性质。

items.meaning: strict adherence to law or to written rules
items.meaningCN: 条文主义；死守法律条文
items.example: Critics say legalism ignores the purpose behind the rule.
items.exampleCN: 批评者说条文主义忽视了规则背后的目的。

latinEntries.meaning: lawful, valid; also reasonable and justified
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合法的、有效的；也指合理正当的（词根仍是 lex“法”）

latinEntries.meaning: the body that has power to make laws
latinEntries.meaningCN: 立法机关（legis 属格 + lator“提出者”）

latinEntries.meaning: faithful to a ruler, country or promise
latinEntries.meaningCN: 忠诚的；同源于 legalis，经法语音变而成，不是英语 legal 的派生

latinEntries.meaning: a special right; originally a law made for an individual
latinEntries.meaningCN: 特权；原指为某个人制定的法律（privus“个人”+ lex“法”）

definition_zh: 合法性；合乎法律的性质；（某一行为或决定的）法律效力
definition_en: the quality or state of being allowed by law, or the question of whether an act, order or body conforms to legal rules
core_image: 一叠文件摊在桌上，红笔沿条文一路打勾，勾到一半停住，那一行就是站不住脚的地方
scene: 委员会整个上午都在追问那条紧急命令究竟站不站得住脚。The committee spent the morning questioning the legality of the emergency order.
sceneCN: 这里 legality 指「某项命令是否符合法律、是否具有法律依据」（第 2 个义项：对具体法令的符合性）；句意为委员会用整个上午追问那条紧急命令的合法性。图中可辨识物件：成叠文件、红笔、条文页眉、问号标记。

pos.zh: 合法性；合乎法律；法律效力（可数时指具体的合法性问题）

derivatives.zh: 法律的；合法的
合法地
非法性；违法行为
使合法化
拘泥法律条文的

senses.title: Lawfulness in general
senses.titleCN: 合乎法律这一性质本身
senses.definition: the quality of being in accordance with law, considered as a general property
senses.definitionCN: 与法律相符这一性质，作为一般属性来看
senses.example: The court's ruling turned on the legality of the search, not on the facts.
senses.exampleCN: 法院的裁决取决于搜查是否合法，而不是事实本身。
senses.why: Formed from legalis 'of the law' plus the quality suffix -itas, the noun names the property itself, the way brightness names the property of being bright.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 legalis「法律的」加表示性质的后缀构成，命名的是性质本身，正如 brightness 命名「亮」这一性质。

senses.title: Conformity with a particular rule
senses.titleCN: 对某一具体法令或命令的符合
senses.definition: the fact of conforming, or failing to conform, to a specific statute, order or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 符合或不符合某一具体法令、命令或程序的事实
senses.example: The committee spent the morning questioning the legality of the emergency order.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会整个上午都在追问那条紧急命令的合法性。
senses.why: Once a rule exists, the interesting question is whether this act matches it, so the noun shifts from a general property to a testable fit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦存在一条规则，真正的问题就是「这个行为是否与它相符」，名词于是从一般属性变为可检验的符合性。

senses.title: Validity of an official act
senses.titleCN: 官方行为或决定在程序上的有效性
senses.definition: the validity of an official decision when measured against the powers that were granted to make it
senses.definitionCN: 把官方决定对照其被授予的权限来衡量时，该决定是否有效
senses.example: Lawyers disputed the legality of a ruling issued after the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们对一份在期限之后作出的裁决是否合法提出争议。
senses.why: An official may act wrongly in two ways, by doing what is forbidden and by acting beyond the power given; legality covers both.
senses.whyCN: 官员可以在两处出错：做被禁止的事，或越过被授予的权力；合法性同时覆盖这两者。

senses.title: Legal standing of a body
senses.titleCN: 某一机构在法律上的地位
senses.definition: the recognised legal existence or status of an organisation, party or government
senses.definitionCN: 某一组织、政党或政府被法律承认的存在或地位
senses.example: Observers asked about the legality of the provisional council.
senses.exampleCN: 观察人士询问该临时委员会在法律上是否成立。
senses.why: A body can exist in fact and still lack legal existence, so the noun is used for the gap between being there and being recognised.
senses.whyCN: 一个机构可以在事实上存在却缺乏法律上的存在，名词因此被用来指「存在于那里」与「被承认」之间的缝隙。

senses.title: Respect for the legal order
senses.definition: the principle that public power should be exercised through law and that everyone, including officials, is bound by it
senses.definitionCN: 主张公共权力应经由法律行使、包括官员在内人人受其约束的原则
senses.example: The report treats legality as a guarantee against arbitrary rule.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把守法原则视为抵御任意统治的保障。
senses.why: The abstract noun can be turned into a value, and then it means not the fit of one act but the commitment to keep measuring acts at all.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词可以转成一个价值，此时它指的不是某一行为的符合，而是坚持对所有行为加以衡量的承诺。

senses.title: The question courts review
senses.titleCN: 法院审查时所称的合法性问题
senses.definition: the issue a court decides when it reviews whether an authority stayed inside its legal powers
senses.definitionCN: 法院在审查某一机关是否停留在其法定权限内时所判定的争点
senses.example: Judicial review separates questions of legality from questions of merit.
senses.exampleCN: 司法审查把合法性问题与是非优劣的问题分开。
senses.why: Judges are not asked whether a decision was wise, only whether it was legally possible, and that narrow question takes the noun.
senses.whyCN: 法官不被问决定是否明智，只被问在法律上是否可能，这个狭窄的问题便承接了这个名词。

senses.title: Lawfulness under international rules
senses.titleCN: 依国际法规则判断的合法性
senses.definition: the conformity of a state's action to treaties, customary rules or a charter
senses.definitionCN: 国家行为对条约、习惯规则或宪章的符合
senses.example: Debate over the legality of the intervention split the assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这次干预是否合法的争论让大会分裂。
senses.why: There is no world statute book, so legality at that level means fit with agreements and accepted practice rather than with one parliament's act.
senses.whyCN: 世界上没有统一的法令全书，因此这一层面的合法性指与协议和公认惯例相符，而非与某一议会的法案相符。

senses.title: Legality as distinct from legitimacy
senses.titleCN: 与「正当性」相区分的合法性
senses.definition: formal conformity to law, considered separately from whether the law or the act is morally accepted
senses.definitionCN: 对法律形式上的符合，与法律或行为是否在道德上被接受分开来看
senses.example: A policy can satisfy legality and still lack legitimacy among the people it affects.
senses.exampleCN: 一项政策可以在形式上合法，却在受影响的人群中缺乏正当性。
senses.why: Political theory needed two words because a ruler may obey every statute and still be rejected, and that gap is exactly what this contrast marks.
senses.whyCN: 政治理论需要两个词，因为统治者可能条条守法却仍被拒斥，这一落差正是该对照所标记的。

intro.en: Legality comes from medieval Latin legalitas, formed on legalis 'of the law', which rests on lex 'law'. English took it through French in the late medieval period.
intro.cn: legality 来自中世纪拉丁 legalitas，由 legalis「法律的」构成，而后者出自 lex「法律」。英语在中世纪后期经法语借入。

items.en: Lex, genitive legis, named an enacted statute rather than justice in the abstract; ius covered the wider idea of right.
items.cn: lex（属格 legis）命名被制定的法令，而非抽象的正义；更宽的权利观念由 ius 承担。

items.en: Source uncertain (root of lex): a link with legere 'to read, gather' is often proposed but not demonstrated, and a derivation from a root meaning 'to lay down' is also argued.
items.cn: 来源不确定（lex 的词根）：与 legere「读、收集」的联系常被提出，但未获证明；也有从表示「立下、放置」的词根派生之说。

items.en: Legalitas was used in medieval Latin for the quality of being lawful, especially of an act or a person's status under canon and civil law.
items.cn: legalitas 在中世纪拉丁语中指合乎法律的性质，尤用于教会法与市民法下的行为或身份。

items.en: The noun reached English through French in the late medieval period, first in the sense of lawfulness in general.
items.cn: 这个名词在中世纪后期经法语进入英语，最初指一般的守法性。

items.en: With written constitutions and judicial review, legality became a testable question about official powers rather than a description of a person.
items.cn: 随着成文宪法与司法审查的出现，合法性从对人的描述变成关于官方权限的可检验问题。

items.en: The earliest English citation is approximate: the medieval borrowing is well attested, but the modern review sense is dated only roughly to the constitutional period.
items.cn: 英语最早书证为约数：中世纪借入一事有充分书证，而现代的审查义只能粗略定在立宪时期。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin family and is the commonest source of error; the second group names neighbouring standards that are often confused with legality.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族的词，也是最常见的出错来源；第二组是常与合法性混淆的相邻标准。

entries.definition: The adjective: allowed by law, or belonging to the field of law.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：法律允许的，或属于法律领域的。

entries.definition: The adverb: in a lawful manner, or judged from the law's angle.
entries.definitionCN: 副词：以合法方式，或从法律角度判断。

entries.definition: The same property negated; it can also name a specific unlawful act.
entries.definitionCN: 同一性质的否定形式；也可指具体的违法行为。

entries.definition: The verb of removing a prohibition, which changes the statute rather than proving conformity to it.
entries.definitionCN: 解除禁令的动词，改变的是法令，而非证明符合法令。

entries.definition: About making statutes, from lex plus latum 'carried'; it describes the source of rules, not their observance.
entries.definitionCN: 关于制定法令，由 lex 加「携带」的过去分词构成；它描述规则的来源，而非遵守。

entries.definition: Acceptance by those governed, resting on consent, tradition or fairness; an act can be lawful and still lack it.
entries.definitionCN: 被治理者的接受，建立在同意、传统或公平之上；一个行为可以合法却仍缺乏它。

entries.definition: Whether an act produces its intended legal effect, which may fail for procedural reasons even when the power existed.
entries.definitionCN: 行为是否产生预期法律效果；即使权限存在，也可能因程序问题而失效。

entries.definition: The everyday synonym, built on the native noun law rather than the Latin one.
entries.definitionCN: 日常同义词，由本族词 law 而非拉丁词构成。

entries.definition: Conformity to the constitution specifically, a narrower and stronger standard than ordinary legality.
entries.definitionCN: 特指对宪法的符合，比一般的合法性更窄也更强。

entries.definition: Correctness by social or professional norms, which law does not enforce.
entries.definitionCN: 依社会或职业规范的正确性，法律并不强制执行。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin law word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「法律」词、真实的同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Lex is Latin for statute, and the quality suffix turns it into the property of conforming, so legality is the fit between act and rule.
normal.cn: lex 是拉丁语「法令」，表性质的后缀把词变成「符合」这一属性，因此合法性就是行为与规则之间的贴合。

normal.en: The family runs legal, legally, legality, illegal, illegality and legalise.
normal.cn: 同族词有 legal、legally、legality、illegal、illegality 与 legalise。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the tested sense: question the legality of, legality review, legality and legitimacy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出被检验的义：质疑……的合法性、合法性审查、合法性与正当性。

normal.en: Latin kept ius for right and lex for statute, which is why English legality never means justice.
normal.cn: 拉丁语用 ius 表权利、用 lex 表法令，因此英语的合法性从不等于正义。

normal.en: The pair legality and legitimacy is the standard way to say 'allowed' versus 'accepted'.
normal.cn: 合法性与正当性这一对，是区分「被允许」与「被接受」的标准说法。

abstract.en: Picture a red pen ticking down a list of clauses and stopping at one line.
abstract.cn: 想象一支红笔沿条款清单一路打勾，到某一行停住。

abstract.en: Picture a building with a legal address but no key that any court would hand over.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋有法定地址、却拿不到任何法院会交付的钥匙的楼。

abstract.en: Picture two identical stamps, one on a treaty and one on a parking ticket.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚一模一样的印章，一枚盖在条约上，一枚盖在停车罚单上。

examples.en: The auditors raised doubts about the legality of the transfer.
examples.cn: 审计人员对这笔转账的合法性提出了疑问。

examples.en: Legality is not the same as popularity.
examples.cn: 合法并不等于受欢迎。

examples.en: The charter sets out the legality of using force in self-defence.
examples.cn: 宪章规定了在自卫中使用武力的合法性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「legal（合法的）+ ity（性质）」——合乎法律的这种性质 → 合法性

root: 拉丁 lex（属格 legis）「法令」（更深词根存疑）→ legalis「法律的」→ 中世纪拉丁 legalitas「合乎法律的性质」→ 法语 → 英语 legality。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one red tick: it marks a property, tests a specific order, checks an official's power, asks whether a body exists in law, becomes a civic value, narrows into a judicial question, crosses into international rules, and finally splits from legitimacy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一道红勾：它标出一种性质，检验一条具体命令，核对官员的权限，追问机构在法律上是否存在，升为公民价值，收窄为司法问题，跨入国际规则，最后与正当性分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red pen running down a page of clauses, stopping where the fit breaks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支红笔沿满页条款向下走，在贴合断掉的地方停住。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND TEST: the abstract quality and the concrete fit are the same measurement at two levels of generality.
branches.cn: 性质与检验：抽象性质与具体符合，是同一次衡量在两个概括层次上。

branches.en: POWER AND EXISTENCE: an act beyond granted power, and a body without legal existence, are two ways of failing the same test.
branches.cn: 权限与存在：越权作出的行为与法律上不存在的机构，是同一种检验的两种失败。

branches.en: THE VALUE: the noun can stop measuring single acts and become a commitment to keep measuring.
branches.cn: 价值：名词可以不再衡量单个行为，而成为一种坚持衡量的承诺。

branches.en: TWO COURTS: a domestic judge asks whether the power existed; international law asks whether the state kept its agreements.
branches.cn: 两座法庭：国内法官问权限是否存在，国际法问国家是否守约。

branches.en: THE SPLIT: legality measures the fit, legitimacy measures the acceptance, and the pair exists because the two can diverge.
branches.cn: 分裂：合法性衡量贴合，正当性衡量接受；这一对之所以存在，正因为两者可以背离。

intro.en: Legality is a Latin law root plus a quality suffix, with the adjective ending still visible inside it.
intro.cn: legality 是一个拉丁「法律」词根加表性质的后缀，形容词词尾仍留在词内。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex, genitive legis, gives legalis, legalitas and legislator; the same root is behind legitimate, though through a different stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lex（属格 legis）衍生 legalis、legalitas 与 legislator；同一词根也在 legitimate 背后，但经另一词干。

items.example: The root names the enacted rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被制定的规则。

items.example: It forms the adjective of law.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示法律的形容词。

items.example: The base adjective of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族的基础形容词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a property noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表性质的名词。

items.example: The noun names the fit, not the rule.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名贴合，而非规则。

items.example: The opposite property, also used for one unlawful act.
items.exampleCN: 相反的性质，也可指一桩违法行为。

items.example: It forms the verb of changing the statute.
items.exampleCN: 它构成修改法令的动词。

items.example: The verb changes the rule, not the fit.
items.exampleCN: 动词改变规则，而非贴合。

items.example: It appears in legislate and legislator.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在「立法」与「立法者」中。

derivatives.zh: 法律的；合法的
合法地
非法性；违法行为
使合法化
拘泥法律条文的

definition_zh: 立法；立法行为；法律法规（总称）；（某一部）法律
definition_en: the making of laws by an authorized body, or the body of laws so made
core_image: 议事厅里逐条朗读、举手表决，散会后书记员把通过的条文装订成厚册
scene: 辩论持续到深夜，反对党仍要求把每一条都念完再表决。Parliament passed legislation that rewrites the funding formula.
sceneCN: 这里 legislation 指立法机关通过的法律（第 2 个义项：法规总称）；句意为议会通过了一项改写拨款公式的法律。

pos.zh: 一部法律（可数，常见于美式用法）

forms.label: 复数（指多部法律，多见于美式用法）

derivatives.zh: 立法（legislation 去后缀构成动词，由产物转指制定过程）
立法的（legislate + -ive「有……性质的」，由动作转指属性）
立法者；议员（legislate + -or「行事者」，由动作转指人）
立法机关（legislate + -ure「机构」，由动作转指机关）

senses.title: The making of laws
senses.definition: the process or act of making laws through an authorized body
senses.definitionCN: 由有权机关制定法律的过程或行为
senses.example: Legislation took eighteen months and three committees.
senses.exampleCN: 立法花了十八个月、经过三个委员会。
senses.why: the Latin noun names the bringing of a law, an act rather than a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本指「把法带来」，是行为而非物品。

senses.title: Laws collectively
senses.definition: the whole body of enacted laws on a subject or in a jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或某一法域已颁行的全部法律
senses.example: Environmental legislation now covers the whole watershed.
senses.exampleCN: 环境法规如今覆盖整个流域。
senses.why: mass-noun use treats statutes as one substance, which is how policy talk usually needs them.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法把诸多法令当作一种物质，政策讨论通常正需要这样。

senses.title: A single statute
senses.definition: one enacted law, countable especially in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 一部已颁行的法律，在美式用法中可数
senses.example: Two legislations were merged into one act.
senses.exampleCN: 两部法令被合并为一项法案。
senses.why: American usage makes the noun countable because each bill becomes a numbered law.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把这个名词可数化，因为每项议案都会成为一部编号法律。

senses.title: The legislative process
senses.definition: the staged procedure of reading, amending and voting that a bill must pass
senses.definitionCN: 议案必须经过的宣读、修正与表决的分阶段程序
senses.example: The rules of legislation favour whoever controls the agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 立法程序偏向掌控议程的一方。
senses.why: procedure is the machinery behind the act, and English uses the same noun for both.
senses.whyCN: 程序是行为背后的机器，英语用同一个名词兼指两者。

senses.title: What a legislature enacts
senses.definition: the output of a parliament or congress, as distinct from rules made by agencies
senses.definitionCN: 议会或国会的产出，区别于行政机关自订的规则
senses.example: Primary legislation needs a vote; guidance does not.
senses.exampleCN: 主要立法需要表决，行政指引则不必。
senses.why: the word marks the source of authority, so it separates parliamentary output from administrative rules.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标示权威来源，因此把议会产出与行政规则分开。

senses.title: Delegated legislation
senses.definition: rules made by a minister or agency under powers granted by a statute
senses.definitionCN: 部长或机关依法律授予的权力制定的规则
senses.example: Delegated legislation fills in technical detail the chamber cannot debate.
senses.exampleCN: 次级立法填补议会无法逐条辩论的技术细节。
senses.why: the word travels with the authority to make law, even when that authority has been lent out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随立法权一同转移，即使该权力是被借出去的。

senses.title: Proposed legislation
senses.definition: a bill or draft still before the chamber, spoken of as future law
senses.definitionCN: 仍在议会审议、被视作未来法律的议案或草案
senses.example: Proposed legislation would cap the fee at ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 拟议立法将把这个费用上限设为百分之十。
senses.why: the word is applied ahead of enactment because the shape of the law is already visible in the draft.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在通过之前就被使用，因为法律的形状在草案里已经可见。

senses.title: Rules for an organization
senses.titleCN: 引申：组织内部规则体系
senses.definition: the formal rules by which a body governs its own members or processes
senses.definitionCN: 某机构管理自身成员或流程的成文规则
senses.example: The society's legislation on conflicts of interest is three pages long.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会关于利益冲突的规则有三页纸。
senses.why: private bodies borrow the word when their rules begin to function like statutes.
senses.whyCN: 私人机构在其规则开始像法令一样运作时，便借用了这个词。

intro.en: Legislation comes from Latin legis latio 'a bringing of a law', from lex 'law' and latio 'a bringing', the noun of latus, the past participle of ferre 'to carry'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: legislation 来自拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」，由 lex「法」与 latio「带来」构成，后者是 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus 的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lex meant 'law, statute, a motion put to the people'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to legere 'to read' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lex 意为「法、法令、提交民众的动议」。其更深来源未得到证明；与 legere「读」的旧联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ferre 'to carry, bring' has the suppletive participle latus, from which latio 'a bringing' is formed; the two verbs were already fused in classical usage.
items.cn: ferre「搬运、带来」的过去分词为异干互补的 latus，由其构成 latio「带来」；两者在古典用法中已合并。

items.en: The phrase legis latio named the bringing of a bill before the assembly, a procedural act rather than the text itself.
items.cn: legis latio 这一说法指把议案带到大会之前的程序性行为，而非文本本身。

items.en: Medieval Latin legislatio generalized the phrase into the making of laws by any authorized body.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 legislatio 把这一说法一般化，指任何有权机关制定法律。

items.en: French législation passed into English in the seventeenth century, first as the act and soon after as the body of laws.
items.cn: 法语 législation 在 17 世纪进入英语，先指立法行为，不久也指法律总体。
