items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not precisely dated, and the origin of lex itself remains unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；lex 本身的来源仍无定论，为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the lex or legisl- stem; group two holds words for laws and for the making of them.
note.cn: 第一组共享 lex 或 legisl- 词干；第二组是关于法律与制定法律的词。

entries.definition: Describing a body or power that makes law; it cannot stand for the laws themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 描述制定法律的机关或权力；不能指法律本身。

entries.definition: The assembly that makes law, formed with -ure 'place or body'; a different thing from the laws it makes.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的议会，由 -ure「场所、机构」构成；与其所制定的法律是两回事。

entries.definition: One member who makes law; the noun names a role, not an output.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的成员之一；指角色，而非产出。

entries.definition: From Latin legitimus 'lawful', built on lex but through a different adjective; it means lawful, not law-making.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 legitimus「合法的」，虽出 lex 却经另一形容词；意为合法，而非立法。

entries.definition: A single rule or the whole body of rules; legislation is the making of it or the output as a mass.
entries.definitionCN: 单条规则或全部规则；legislation 指制定过程或作为总体的产出。

entries.definition: A single law passed by a legislature, countable and technical; legislation is the wider mass noun.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的单项法律，可数且技术化；legislation 是更宽的总称。

entries.definition: Detailed rules issued by an agency under a statute, usually not requiring a parliamentary vote.
entries.definitionCN: 机关依法令发布的细则，通常不经议会表决。

entries.definition: A draft law still under consideration; legislation names what it becomes, or the process of making it.
entries.definitionCN: 仍在审议的草案；legislation 指它最终成为的东西，或制定它的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: legis latio: the bringing of a law, so the word began as a motion carried forward.
normal.cn: legis latio：把法带来，因此这个词本是一项被送上前的动议。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislator, legislature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split act from output: pass legislation, delegated legislation, environmental legislation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出行为与产出：通过立法、授权立法、环境立法。

normal.en: Contrast the pair: a bill is the draft, legislation is the making and the mass of laws.
normal.cn: 对照这一对：bill 是草案，legislation 是制定过程与法律总体。

normal.en: Watch the false friend legitimate: lawful, but built on a different adjective of lex.
normal.cn: 提防假朋友 legitimate：意为合法，却由 lex 的另一形容词构成。

abstract.en: Picture a text carried by hand across a hall before anyone votes on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文本在被人手捧着穿过大厅，之后才有人表决。

abstract.en: Picture shelves that grow a new thick volume every session.
abstract.cn: 想象书架每开一次会就多一本厚册。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that must be read aloud before it can bind anyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则必须先被大声读出，才能约束任何人。

examples.en: The state's legislation on groundwater is older than its mapping.
examples.cn: 该州关于地下水的立法比水文测绘还要早。

examples.en: Delegated legislation filled in the standards the chamber left blank.
examples.cn: 次级立法填上了议会留白的技术标准。

examples.en: Industry lobbied against the proposed legislation for two years.
examples.cn: 业界游说反对这项拟议立法达两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: legis（法）+ lation（带来）＝ 把法带到台面上；记「念一遍、改一遍、举一次手」。

root: 拉丁 legis latio「把法带来」= lex「法」（更深来源不确定，与 legere「读」的联系仅为假说）+ latio「带来」（来自 ferre「搬运」的过去分词 latus）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a bill from act to archive: making law, the mass of law, one statute, the procedure, parliamentary output, delegated rules, drafts not yet passed, and the rules of a private body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一项议案从行为走到档案：立法、法律总体、单部法律、程序、议会产出、授权规则、尚未通过的草案，以及私人机构的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a text read aloud, amended, voted on, then bound into a thick volume.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份文本被朗读、修正、表决，最后装订进厚册。

branches.en: ACT AND MASS: the making of law, then the whole body it accumulates into.
branches.cn: 行为与总体：先制定，再累积成整体。

branches.en: ONE VOLUME: the countable unit inside the mass.
branches.cn: 单册：总体之中的可数单位。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: procedure at work, and the authority that makes its output law.
branches.cn: 机器：程序在运转，以及使其产成为法律的权威。

branches.en: LENT POWER: rule-making handed to ministers and agencies.
branches.cn: 借出的权力：规则制定权交到部长与机关手里。

branches.en: BEFORE AND AFTER THE HALL: drafts spoken of as law, and private bodies drafting their own.
branches.cn: 大厅前后：草案已被当作法律谈论，私人机构也自订规则。

intro.en: Legislation joins a Latin noun for law to a Latin noun for bringing, and the second element still appears in English words of transfer.
intro.cn: legislation 把拉丁语「法」的名词与「带来」的名词接在一起，后一成分仍出现在英语的转移类词中。

latinIntro.en: Lex supplies legal, legitimate and legislate; latus and ferre supply transfer, refer and relate.
latinIntro.cn: lex 衍生 legal、legitimate、legislate；latus 与 ferre 衍生 transfer、refer、relate。

items.example: Lex is the root of legal and legislate.
items.exampleCN: lex 是 legal 与 legislate 的词根。

items.example: Its participle latus hides inside latio.
items.exampleCN: 其分词 latus 藏在 latio 里。

items.example: Legis latio is the bringing of a bill.
items.exampleCN: legis latio 就是把议案带来。

items.example: The chamber legislates twice a year.
Legislation followed the report by a year.
items.exampleCN: 报告之后一年才有了立法。

items.example: The legislator read the amendment aloud.
items.exampleCN: 立法者大声读了修正案。

items.example: A legitimate claim differs from a popular one.
items.exampleCN: 合法的诉求与受欢迎的诉求不同。

definition_zh: 立法的；立法机关的；有立法权的；由立法设立的
definition_en: relating to the making of laws or to the body that makes them
core_image: 一间半圆形的议事厅，座位上标着选区名，中央的书记员正在点票
scene: 修稿一直改到表决前一小时，主席仍要求先算清票数。The legislative committee rewrote the clause before the final vote.
sceneCN: 这里 legislative 指属于立法机关及其程序的（第 1 个义项：与立法机关有关）；句意为立法委员会在最终表决前重写了该条款。

pos.zh: 立法的；立法机关的；有立法权的

derivatives.zh: 立法；法规（legislate + -ion「行为或结果」，由属性转指其所指的过程与产物）
立法机关（legislate + -ure「机构」，由属性转指持有它的机关）
立法者（legislate + -or「行事者」，由属性转指人）
立法（由 legislative 的词干逆构，由属性转指行为）

senses.title: Of the law-making body
senses.definition: belonging to the assembly that makes laws, as opposed to the executive or the courts
senses.definitionCN: 属于制定法律的议会，与行政或法院相对
senses.example: The legislative calendar leaves little room for debate.
senses.exampleCN: 立法日程几乎没给辩论留空间。
senses.why: the suffix -ive marks a body's characteristic function, so the adjective names the branch by what it does.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 标示某机构特有的职能，因此形容词按它做什么来命名这一分支。

senses.title: Holding the power to make law
senses.definition: possessing authority to enact binding law
senses.definitionCN: 持有颁行有约束力法律的权威
senses.example: Legislative power cannot be delegated without limits.
senses.exampleCN: 立法权不能无限制地授出。
senses.why: power is what separates law-making from advising, so the adjective attaches to authority itself.
senses.whyCN: 权力把立法与建议区分开，因此形容词也直接接在权威上。

senses.title: Of the procedure
senses.definition: concerning the steps of reading, amending and voting on a bill
senses.definitionCN: 关于议案的宣读、修正与表决步骤
senses.example: A legislative deadlock can outlast a session.
senses.exampleCN: 立法僵局可以跨会期延续。
senses.why: procedure is the visible part of law-making, so the adjective routinely describes it.
senses.whyCN: 程序是立法最可见的部分，因此形容词经常描述它。

senses.title: Created by statute
senses.definition: established by an act of a legislature rather than by administrative decision
senses.definitionCN: 由立法机关的法令、而非行政决定设立
senses.example: The ombudsman is a legislative creation, not a ministerial one.
senses.exampleCN: 监察专员是立法设立的，而非部长设立的。
senses.why: the adjective can mark origin, telling us which kind of authority brought a body into being.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可标示来源，说明是哪一类权威使某机构得以成立。

senses.title: Law-making in character
senses.definition: having the character of law-making even outside a parliament, as with a treaty clause
senses.definitionCN: 即使不在议会之内，也带立法性质，如条约条款
senses.example: The council's vote had a legislative effect on the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会的投票对整个地区产生了立法效果。
senses.why: the adjective can describe an effect rather than a body, since making binding rules is what defines it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可描述效果而非机构，因为「制定有约束力的规则」才是它的定义特征。

senses.title: Separated from executive and judicial
senses.definition: naming one of the three functions of government in the doctrine of separation of powers
senses.definitionCN: 在三权分立学说中指政府三大职能之一
senses.example: Legislative independence was the point of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 立法独立正是这场改革的要点。
senses.why: the modern sense is defined by contrast: legislative is whatever the other two branches are not.
senses.whyCN: 现代义靠对照定义：立法者就是另外两支所不是的那个。

senses.title: Of members or elections
senses.titleCN: 立法机关成员的、议员选举的
senses.definition: concerning the members of a legislature or the elections that seat them
senses.definitionCN: 关于立法机关成员或使其当选的选举
senses.example: Legislative elections were moved up by six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 立法机关选举提前了六周。
senses.why: metonymy lets the branch stand for the people in it, a very common journalistic shorthand.
senses.whyCN: 转喻让这一分支代表其中的人，是新闻语体极常见的简称。

senses.title: Legislative history
senses.titleCN: 立法沿革资料（用于解释法条）
senses.definition: the record of debates, drafts and reports used by courts to interpret a statute
senses.definitionCN: 法院解释法条时所用的辩论、草案与报告记录
senses.example: Judges read the legislative record before ruling on intent.
senses.exampleCN: 法官在裁定立法意图之前先读立法记录。
senses.why: English gives this technical sense to the adjective because the material belongs to the law-making stage.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个技术义交给形容词，因为该材料属于立法阶段。

intro.en: Legislative is the adjective of legislation, from Latin lex 'law' and latus 'carried', the participle of ferre. The English adjective appears in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: legislative 是 legislation 的形容词，来自拉丁 lex「法」与 latus「被搬运的」，后者是 ferre 的分词。英语形容词见于 17 世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lex 'law' has no established deeper origin; the old suggestion of a link to legere 'to read' is a hypothesis only.
items.cn: lex「法」的更深来源未得到证明；与 legere「读」有关的旧说仅为假说。

items.en: Latus is the suppletive participle of ferre 'to carry'; legis latio named the bringing of a bill before the assembly.
items.cn: latus 是 ferre「搬运」的异干互补分词；legis latio 指把议案带到大会之前。

items.en: Legislatio generalized the phrase to law-making, and its adjective legislativus described what belongs to that function.
items.cn: legislatio 把这一说法一般化为立法，其形容词 legislativus 描述属于该职能之物。

items.en: French législatif passed into English in the seventeenth century, at first in writing on the separation of powers.
items.cn: 法语 législatif 在 17 世纪进入英语，最初见于论三权分立的著述。

items.en: With the spread of written constitutions the adjective became a fixed label for one branch, always defined against the executive and the courts.
items.cn: 随着成文宪法的传播，这个形容词成为某一分支的固定标签，总在与行政、法院的对照中被定义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not exactly dated, and the origin of lex remains unsettled, so older forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；lex 的来源仍无定论，为其提出的更早形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the legisl- stem; group two holds adjectives of government functions.
note.cn: 第一组共享 legisl- 词干；第二组是政府各职能的形容词。

entries.definition: The act or the body of laws; the adjective only describes what belongs to that act.
entries.definitionCN: 行为或法律总体；形容词只描述属于该行为之物。

entries.definition: The body that legislates; a legislative committee belongs to it rather than being it.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的机构；立法委员会属于它，而不等于它。

entries.definition: From legitimus 'lawful'; it shares the lex root but means permitted, not legislative.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 legitimus「合法的」；共享 lex 词根，却意为获准的，而非立法的。

entries.definition: A member who makes law; the adjective would describe the member's work, not the member.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律的成员；形容词描述其工作，而非其本人。

entries.definition: Of a parliament's rules and manners; legislative concerns law-making power, which is narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 指议会的规则与礼仪；legislative 关注立法权，范围更窄。

entries.definition: Created or required by a particular act; legislative describes the function rather than the binding force.
entries.definitionCN: 由某部法令创设或要求；legislative 描述职能，而非约束力。

entries.definition: Of the branch that carries out policy; it is defined by contrast with legislative and judicial.
entries.definitionCN: 指执行政策的分支；它与立法、司法相对而被定义。

entries.definition: The everyday compound for the same idea; legislative is its formal, constitutional counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 同一意思的日常复合词；legislative 是其正式、宪制性的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: legis latio 'bringing of a law' plus -ive: having the character of that bringing.
normal.cn: legis latio「把法带来」加 -ive：带有那种「带来」的性质。

normal.en: The family runs legislate, legislation, legislative, legislator, legislature.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 legislate、legislation、legislative、legislator、legislature。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branch: legislative power, legislative committee, legislative agenda.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一分支：立法权、立法委员会、立法议程。

normal.en: Three adjectives divide the state: legislative, executive, judicial.
normal.cn: 三个形容词把国家切开：立法的、行政的、司法的。

normal.en: The technical phrase legislative history sends courts back to the debates.
normal.cn: 术语 legislative history 把法院送回辩论记录。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the only thing made is sentences that bind people outside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，里面唯一制造的东西是能约束屋外之人的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a hall that later requires thousands of hands to obey.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里举起的一只手，日后要成千上万只手服从。

abstract.en: Picture three pillars, and the left one is always described by what the other two are not.
abstract.cn: 想象三根柱子，左边那根总是靠另外两根「不是什么」来描述。

examples.en: The legislative branch cannot enforce its own statutes.
examples.cn: 立法分支无法自己执行其法令。

examples.en: A legislative fix would take a full session.
examples.cn: 用立法方式修补需要整整一个会期。

examples.en: The court consulted the legislative record before ruling.
examples.cn: 法院在裁定前查考了立法记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: legis（法）+ lat（带来）+ ive（……的）＝ 把法带来的那一支；记「只造规则，不管执行」。

root: 拉丁 lex「法」（更深来源不确定，与 legere「读」的联系仅为假说）+ latus「被搬运的」（ferre「搬运」的分词）+ 形容词后缀 -ive。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one function from outside: the body that makes law, the power it holds, its procedure, what it creates, its effect elsewhere, its place in the division of powers, its members, and the record it leaves for courts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从外部描述同一职能：制定法律的机关、它持有的权力、它的程序、它创设之物、它在别处的效果、它在分权中的位置、它的成员，以及它留给法院的记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand in a chamber that turns a sentence into a rule binding those outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：议事厅里举起的一只手，把一句话变成约束厅外之人的规则。

branches.en: BODY AND POWER: the assembly, and the authority that makes its words binding.
branches.cn: 机关与权力：议会，以及使其言语有约束力的权威。

branches.en: PROCEDURE AND PRODUCT: the steps, then the bodies and rules those steps create.
branches.cn: 程序与产物：先是步骤，再是这些步骤所创设的机构与规则。

branches.en: EFFECT WITHOUT A CHAMBER: legislative quality can attach to a treaty or a council vote.
branches.cn: 无厅之效：立法性质也可附在条约或委员会表决上。

branches.en: DEFINED BY CONTRAST: the branch is what the executive and the courts are not.
branches.cn: 靠对照定义：这一分支就是行政与法院所不是的。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PAPER: the members elected, and the record they leave behind.
branches.cn: 人与纸：选出的成员，以及他们留下的记录。

intro.en: Legislative is built from a Latin law noun, a Latin participle and an English adjective suffix, so each part can be read alone.
intro.cn: legislative 由拉丁「法」名词、拉丁分词与英语形容词后缀构成，每一部分都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Lex gives legal, legitimate and legislate; latus and ferre give transfer, refer, relate and translate.
latinIntro.cn: lex 衍生 legal、legitimate、legislate；latus 与 ferre 衍生 transfer、refer、relate、translate。

items.exampleCN: lex 支撑 legal 与 legitimate。

items.example: The participle supplies the second half of legislation.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了 legislation 的后半。

items.meaning: tending to, having the character of
items.example: The suffix turns a function into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一种职能变成形容词。

items.example: Only the chamber may legislate here.
items.exampleCN: 此处只有该院可以立法。

items.example: The legislature met for six weeks.

items.exampleCN: 该问题是以立法方式处理的。

items.example: One legislator held the floor for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 一位议员占了一个小时的发言。

definition_zh: 合法的；合理的；正当的；正统的；婚生的
definition_en: allowed by law, supported by good reason, genuine and valid, or rightful by established authority
core_image: 市政厅窗口前，办事员把执照递到申请人手上，逐条核对经营范围和地址
scene: 市政厅窗口前，办事员把执照递到申请人手上，逐条核对经营范围和地址。Only businesses with a legitimate licence may operate here.
sceneCN: 这里指依法获准的（第 1 个义项：合法的）；句意为只有持有合法执照的企业才能在此经营。

pos.zh: 合法的；合理的；正当的；正统的；婚生的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「合法性；正当性」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词尾构成，义为「合法地；正当地」
由该形容词加表示「使成为」的动词尾构成，义为「使合法化」
由同族动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「合法化；认领」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「非法的；不正当的」

senses.title: Allowed by law
senses.definition: permitted by the legal order of a country or institution
senses.definitionCN: 为一个国家或机构的法律秩序所允许
senses.example: Only a legitimate licence allows you to trade here.
senses.exampleCN: 只有合法执照才允许你在此经营。
senses.why: The Latin root is law itself, so the first sense is simply conformity with what the law permits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根就是「法律」，所以第一个义项就是与法律所允许的一致。

senses.title: Supported by good reason
senses.definition: justified by evidence or by a fair argument, even where no law is involved
senses.definitionCN: 由证据或公平论证证明为正当，即使不涉及法律
senses.example: Parents have a legitimate concern about the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 家长对新课表有合理的关切。
senses.why: Law is the model of what is acceptable, and the word extends to whatever would pass a fair test of reason.
senses.whyCN: 法律是「可接受」的范本，这个词于是扩展到任何能通过公正理性检验的事物。

senses.title: Genuine and valid
senses.definition: of a document, claim or result that is authentic and stands up to checking
senses.definitionCN: 指文件、主张或结果真实且经得起核查
senses.example: The archive held a legitimate copy of the original map.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆藏有一份真实有效的原图副本。
senses.why: A forged document is illegitimate even when no statute is named, because authenticity is a kind of law.
senses.whyCN: 伪造文件即使不涉及具体法条也是不正当的，因为真实性本身是一种法则。

senses.title: Born to married parents
senses.definition: in older legal language, of a child born within a recognized marriage
senses.definitionCN: 旧法律用语中指在获认可的婚姻中出生的孩子
senses.example: The old will named only the legitimate son as heir.
senses.exampleCN: 那份旧遗嘱只指定婚生儿子为继承人。
senses.why: Marriage was once the legal form that made a birth regular, so the word applied to the child as well as the union.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻曾是使出生合乎规范的法定形式，因此这个词既用于婚姻，也用于孩子。

senses.title: Rightful by established authority
senses.definition: of a ruler or government whose right to rule is accepted rather than merely seized
senses.definitionCN: 指统治者或政府的统治权被承认，而不只是被夺取
senses.example: The old dynasty was still regarded as the legitimate ruler of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 旧王朝仍被视为该省的合法统治者。
senses.why: Power becomes authority when it can point to a recognized line, and the word names that recognized line.
senses.whyCN: 权力在能指向一条被承认的谱系时成为权威，而这个词命名的正是那条被承认的谱系。

senses.title: Of lawful business activity
senses.definition: of trade, work or profit that is registered, taxed and open to inspection
senses.definitionCN: 指登记、纳税并接受检查的贸易、工作或收益
senses.example: The family ran a legitimate shipping business for three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人合法经营航运生意达三代之久。
senses.why: Commerce needed a word to separate licensed trade from smuggling, and the legal sense did the work.
senses.whyCN: 商业需要一个词把持牌贸易与走私区分开，而「合法」这一义项正好承担了这个功能。

senses.title: Of a fair question or worry
senses.definition: of a doubt or objection that deserves an answer rather than dismissal
senses.definitionCN: 指值得回答而不该被驳回的怀疑或反对
senses.example: It is legitimate to ask where the money went.
senses.exampleCN: 追问这笔钱去了哪里是合理的。
senses.why: A question is legitimate when it has a right to be heard, and rights are the shadow of law behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 一个问题在有权被听见时就是合理的，而权利正是这个词背后法律的影子。

senses.title: Of a government with accepted title
senses.titleCN: 具有被承认资格的正统政府
senses.definition: of a regime recognized by its own people or by other states as properly constituted
senses.definitionCN: 指被本国人民或其他国家承认其组建正当的政权
senses.example: Foreign offices argued over which cabinet was legitimate.
senses.exampleCN: 各国外交部门争论哪一个内阁才是正统的。
senses.why: Recognition is the international form of law, and a government without it is called illegitimate even if it holds the capital.
senses.whyCN: 承认是法律在国际层面的形式，缺少承认的政府即使占据首都也被称为不正当。

senses.title: Of a claim one is entitled to make
senses.definition: of a demand that rests on a right rather than on force or favour
senses.definitionCN: 指依据权利而非武力或恩惠提出的要求
senses.example: The workers had a legitimate claim to the unpaid wages.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们对未付工资有正当的主张权。
senses.why: A claim is legitimate when it can be traced to an entitlement, which is again law in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 主张在能追溯到一项权利时就是正当的，这又是微缩的法律。

intro.en: Legitimate comes from Latin legitimatus, the past participle of legitimare, to make lawful, from legitimus, lawful, from lex, law.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 legitimatus，即 legitimare「使合法」的过去分词，而 legitimare 出自 legitimus「合法的」，其根为 lex「法律」。

items.en: Lex meant law or statute, and its stem legis appears in legal, legislate and legitimacy alike.
items.cn: lex 意为法律或法令，其词干 legis 同时出现在 legal、legislate 与 legitimacy 中。

items.en: The adjective meant lawful or according to law, and it could describe a person, a claim or a birth.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为合法的或依法的，可形容人、主张或出生。

items.en: The verb meant to make lawful or to declare lawful, used of wills, marriages and offices.
items.cn: 这个动词意为使合法或宣布合法，曾用于遗嘱、婚姻与职位。

items.en: French carried the adjective to English, which kept the legal core while widening it to reason and authenticity.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词带给英语，英语保留法律核心，同时把它拓宽到理性与真实性。

items.en: English used the word for lawful births and lawful rulers before it used it for fair arguments; the date of the widening is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语先用它讲婚生与合法统治者，之后才用它讲公正论证；这一拓宽的年代不确定。

items.en: Today the word often means simply reasonable, as in a legitimate question, with the legal sense still underneath.
items.cn: 今天这个词常只表示「合理」，如「合理的疑问」，但法律义仍在底下。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like legitimate; the second group names neighbouring ideas of law and fairness.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 legitimate 相近；第二组是与「法律、公正」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The quality of being lawful or accepted as rightful.
entries.definitionCN: 指合法或被承认为正当的性质。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a lawful or justified way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以合法或有正当理由的方式。

entries.definition: To make something lawful or acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事物合法或可接受。

entries.definition: To make laws; it shares the law root but is not formed from legitimate.
entries.definitionCN: 指制定法律；共享法律词根，但并非由本词派生。

entries.definition: Property left by will; it looks close but comes from a word for a commission or bequest.
entries.definitionCN: 指遗嘱留下的财产；形近，但来自意为「委托、遗赠」的词。

entries.definition: Permitted by statute, the plainest member of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 指为成文法所允许，是这组词中最朴素的。

entries.definition: Relating to law or allowed by it, often used of procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 指与法律有关或为法律所允许，常指程序。

entries.definition: Officially acceptable because the required conditions are met.
entries.definitionCN: 指因满足所需条件而获正式接受。

entries.definition: Shown to have a good reason behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被证明背后有充分理由。

entries.definition: Holding a position or property by proper title.
entries.definitionCN: 指凭正当名分持有职位或财产。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the law root, the three layers of the word and the phrases that keep them apart.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「法律」词根、这个词的三层意思，以及区分这三层的搭配。

normal.en: The root is lex, law, so legitimate starts from what the law allows and then widens to what reason allows.
normal.cn: 词根意为「法律」，所以这个词从「法律允许」出发，再扩展到「理性允许」。

normal.en: Legislate and legal share the root but are different words, not derivatives of legitimate.
normal.cn: 表示「立法」与「法律的」同族词共享词根，却是另外的词，不是本词的派生词。

normal.en: A legitimate licence is lawful, a legitimate question is reasonable, a legitimate king is rightful.
normal.cn: 合法的执照、合理的疑问、正统的国王，三层意思各自清楚。

normal.en: The noun legitimacy is the abstract form used in politics and in arguments about proof.
normal.cn: 名词形式是用于政治与证据争论的抽象说法。

normal.en: Illegitimate simply adds the negative prefix and denies all three layers at once.
normal.cn: 否定形式只是加上否定前缀，一次否定三层意思。

abstract.en: Legitimacy is the story power tells about why it should be obeyed.
abstract.cn: 正当性是权力讲述的、关于自己为何该被服从的故事。

abstract.en: The word quietly moves from statutes to feelings, because people want their worries to have standing.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄从法条移到感受，因为人希望自己的担忧拥有地位。

abstract.en: To call something legitimate is to say it has a right to exist, not merely a permission.
abstract.cn: 称某事正当，是说它有存在的权利，而不只是有许可。

examples.en: The commission asked whether the election had produced a legitimate government.
examples.cn: 委员会询问这场选举是否产生了正统政府。

examples.en: There is a legitimate reason to delay the launch until the tests finish.
examples.cn: 把发布推迟到测试结束是有正当理由的。

examples.en: Only legitimate copies carry the printer's mark on the last page.
examples.cn: 只有正版副本的末页才带印刷商标记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「利己提马特」——凡事「利己」又「提」得出「马」上能查的凭据，才算合法正当

root: 拉丁语 legitimatus（legitimare「使合法」的过去分词）← legitimus「合法的」← lex, legis「法律」。同根有 legal、legislate、legitimacy；legacy 形近但来自「遗赠」义，不同源。三层义（合法、合理、正统）由法律义向外扩展；扩展年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses arrange three layers: law (licence, business, birth), reason (concern, question, claim) and recognized title (ruler, government, authentic document).
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项排成三层：法律（执照、经营、婚生）、理性（关切、疑问、主张）与被承认的名分（统治者、政府、真实文件）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clerk checking a licence line by line against the register.
core.cn: 核心意象：办事员把执照逐条对照登记册。

branches.en: THE LICENSED BRANCH: what the statute allows and the trade that is registered and taxed.
branches.cn: 持牌分支：成文法允许之事，以及登记纳税的经营。

branches.en: THE REASONABLE BRANCH: a fair worry and a question that deserves an answer.
branches.cn: 合理分支：公平的担忧，以及值得回答的疑问。

branches.en: THE PROOF BRANCH: an authentic copy and a claim backed by an entitlement.
branches.cn: 凭据分支：真实副本，以及有权利支撑的主张。

branches.en: THE BIRTH BRANCH: the old legal sense of a child born within marriage.
branches.cn: 出生分支：婚内所生子女的旧法律义。

branches.en: THE TITLE BRANCH: a ruler and a cabinet whose right to rule is recognized.
branches.cn: 名分分支：统治权被承认的君主与内阁。

intro.en: Legitimate is a Latin law word that English widened from statutes to reason, with a productive family on both sides.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁法律词，英语把它从法条拓宽到理性，两侧都有一族能产的派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex and its stem legis supply the root; legitimus, legitimare and legitimatus supply the forms English borrowed or imitated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lex 及其词干 legis 提供词根；legitimus、legitimare 与 legitimatus 提供英语借用或仿造的形式。

items.example: The root is short but stands under a large family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根很短，却支撑着一大族词。

items.example: The stem appears in legal and legislate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在表示「法律的」与「立法」的同族词中。

items.example: It could describe a person or a claim.
Wills and marriages were its objects.
items.exampleCN: 遗嘱与婚姻曾是它的对象。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.example: It lets the same form serve as adjective and verb.
items.exampleCN: 它让同一形式兼作形容词与动词。
它构成表示「合法性」的名词。
它构成表示「非法的」的否定形容词。
它构成表示「使合法化」的动词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「合法性；正当性」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词尾构成，义为「合法地；正当地」
由该形容词加表示「使成为」的动词尾构成，义为「使合法化」
由同族动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「合法化；认领」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「非法的；不正当的」

definition_zh: 闲暇；空闲时间；休闲活动；悠闲；休闲（作定语）
definition_en: time free from work or duties, the activities that fill it, and the relaxed manner that such time allows
core_image: 安静午后的一张空藤椅，旁边放着一杯还冒着热气的茶
scene: 周末的午后，会议与邮件都停了，阳台上的藤椅空着，等一个人端着茶坐下来。Long afternoons of leisure left him free to read whatever he liked.
sceneCN: 这里是「空闲时间」（第 1 个义项：不必工作的自由时间）；句意为漫长的闲暇午后让他能随心读书。图中可辨识物件：阳台藤椅、茶杯、翻开的书。

pos.zh: 闲暇；空闲时间；休闲活动

derivatives.zh: 由 leisure 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「从容的；不慌不忙的」
由 leisure 加 -ed 构成，义为「有大量空闲时间的」
由 leisure 与 wear 复合而成，义为「休闲服饰」

senses.title: Time free from work or duty
senses.definition: time when you are not working and may choose for yourself what to do
senses.definitionCN: 不必工作、可以由自己决定做什么的那段时间
senses.example: She has little leisure during the exam season.
senses.exampleCN: 考试季她几乎没有空闲时间。
senses.why: Latin licere meant to be permitted, so leisure began as permitted time, the hours no duty can claim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licere 意为「被允许」，leisure 最初指被允许自由支配的时间，也就是没有职责占用的那几个小时。

senses.title: Activities enjoyed in that free time
senses.definition: the things people choose to do for pleasure when work is finished
senses.definitionCN: 工作结束后人们为了愉快而选择去做的事情
senses.example: Reading and cycling are his favourite forms of leisure.
senses.exampleCN: 读书和骑车是他最喜欢的休闲方式。
senses.why: Once free hours exist they must be filled, so the word slides from the empty time to the chosen activity that occupies it.
senses.whyCN: 空闲的小时一旦存在，就必然被填满，于是词义从「空白的时间」滑向占用这段时间的自选活动。

senses.title: An unhurried, easy manner
senses.definition: a relaxed way of acting, with no pressure of time and no need to rush
senses.definitionCN: 不受时间压迫、不必赶的轻松做事方式
senses.example: He answered the questions at his leisure.
senses.exampleCN: 他不慌不忙地回答了问题。
senses.why: Time that carries no deadline produces a manner without hurry, so at leisure comes to describe the calm inside the free hours.
senses.whyCN: 没有截止期限的时间会带来不赶的态度，于是 at leisure 用来描述空闲时间里那种从容的心境。

senses.title: Placed before a noun: made for free time
senses.definition: used in front of another noun for places, clothes or industries serving people at leisure
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，指服务于闲暇之人的场所、衣物或产业
senses.example: The town opened a new leisure centre last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇去年春天新开了一家休闲中心。
senses.why: A noun naming free time easily turns into a label on the things built for it, which is why leisure attaches to centres, wear and whole industries.
senses.whyCN: 表示空闲时间的名词很容易变成「为其建造之物」的标签，所以 leisure 能贴在中心、服饰乃至整个产业前面。

intro.en: Leisure comes from a Latin verb of permission and reached English through French, still carrying the idea of hours that nobody else can claim.
intro.cn: leisure 源自拉丁语中表示「允许」的动词，经法语进入英语，至今仍带着「无人能占用的时间」这层意思。

items.en: Licere meant to be allowed or permitted, and it named what a person was free to do.
items.cn: licere 意为「被允许、获准」，指一个人可以自由去做的事。

items.en: Its noun licentia named permission or freedom, the state of being allowed.
items.cn: 其名词 licentia 表示许可或自由，即「获准的状态」。

items.en: Old French shaped the verb as leisir, which meant both to be allowed and the free time that followed.
items.cn: 古法语把动词写作 leisir，既表示「被允许」，也指随之而来的空闲时间。

items.en: Middle English used leisir, later spelled leisure, for time at one's own disposal.
items.cn: 中古英语用 leisir（后写作 leisure）指由自己支配的时间。

items.en: Modern English keeps leisure for free time and extends it to leisure activities, leisure wear and the leisure industry.
items.cn: 现代英语用 leisure 指空闲时间，并扩展到休闲活动、休闲服饰与休闲产业。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same Latin verb of permission; the near-meaning group collects words for spare hours and rest.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「允许」动词上的派生形式；近义组收表示空闲与休息的词。

entries.definition: Acting or moving without hurry.
entries.definitionCN: 不慌不忙的；从容的。

entries.definition: Having plenty of free time, usually through wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 有大量空闲时间的，通常因富裕。

entries.definition: Allowed by law; the opposite of illicit.
entries.definitionCN: 法律允许的；illicit 的反义词。

entries.definition: Official permission to do something, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 官方许可，来自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Time left over after work or duties.
entries.definitionCN: 工作或职责之外剩下的时间。

entries.definition: Resting and letting tension go.
entries.definitionCN: 休息，让紧张消退。

entries.definition: Activities done for enjoyment outside work.
entries.definitionCN: 工作之外为消遣而做的活动。

entries.definition: The state of not working, often with a hint of disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 不做事的状态，常带一点贬义。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for being allowed, and its family keeps returning to permission, free hours and the easy manner they produce.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「获准」的拉丁动词上，同族词反复回到许可、空闲时间以及由此产生的从容态度。

normal.en: Licere in Latin means to be allowed, so leisure is time you are permitted to spend as you wish.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 licere 意为被允许，所以 leisure 是可以随自己支配的获准时间。

normal.en: Old French leisir dropped its verb ending and became leisure, keeping both the permission and the free hours.
normal.cn: 古法语 leisir 去掉动词词尾后成为 leisure，同时保留「许可」和「空闲时间」两层意思。

normal.en: Leisurely adds -ly to leisure, describing the unhurried manner of someone inside free time.
normal.cn: leisurely 在 leisure 后加 -ly，形容人处在空闲时间里的从容样子。

normal.en: Leisure wear joins leisure to wear, clothing for hours when no uniform is required.
normal.cn: leisure wear 把 leisure 与 wear 连起来，指不必穿制服的时段所穿的衣服。

normal.en: The phrase is at leisure, not in leisure, because you sit inside your own free time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 at leisure 而不是 in leisure，因为人坐在自己的空闲时间里。

abstract.en: A word that first meant permission reminds us that free time is not empty space but time granted to us.
abstract.cn: 一个最初表示「许可」的词提醒人：空闲不是空白，而是被准许使用的时光。

abstract.en: Leisure links restful hours with a calm manner, suggesting that how we spend time shapes how we carry ourselves.
abstract.cn: leisure 把休息的时段与从容的态度连在一起，说明怎样花时间会影响人的举止。

abstract.en: When leisure becomes an industry, the very hours once free now have goods built around them.
abstract.cn: 当 leisure 变成一种产业，原本自由的时段周围就长出了专门为它制造的商品。

examples.en: She has little leisure during the exam season.
examples.cn: 考试季她几乎没有空闲时间。

examples.en: Reading and cycling are his favourite forms of leisure.
examples.cn: 读书和骑车是他最喜欢的休闲方式。

examples.en: He answered the questions at his leisure.
examples.cn: 他不慌不忙地回答了问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来这儿」——有空的时候，来这儿坐坐；记住 leisure 是空闲、闲暇。

root: 拉丁语 licere（被允许）→ 拉丁名词 licentia（许可）→ 古法语 leisir（获准的空闲）→ 中古英语 leisure；同族词多与「许可、自由」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is permitted free time; from it grow the activities that fill those hours, the unhurried manner they allow, and the attributive use for things made for them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被允许自由支配的时间」；由此长出填充这些时间的活动、随之而来的从容态度，以及修饰休闲事物的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair on a quiet afternoon, waiting for someone with nowhere else to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：安静午后的一张空椅子，等一个无别处可去的人。

branches.en: a clock with no appointment marked on it
branches.cn: 一只没有记下任何约会的钟

branches.en: a bicycle leaning against a park bench
branches.cn: 靠在公园长椅上的自行车

branches.en: a town building named after free hours
branches.cn: 以闲暇时光命名的小镇建筑

branches.en: a man answering slowly, with no deadline
branches.cn: 不赶时间、从容作答的人

branches.en: a shop window full of clothes for weekends
branches.cn: 橱窗里摆满周末穿的休闲衣

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of permission and its noun, reshaped by French, then extended by English suffixes into a manner and a garment.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示许可的拉丁动词及其名词支撑，经法语改写，再由英语后缀扩展出「态度」和「衣物」。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 长度；长度单位；时长；程度；一段
definition_en: the measurement of something from end to end, its duration in time, the extent to which something is carried out, and a piece cut from something long
core_image: 卷尺从墙角拉到另一头，刻度停在木板的边缘
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉到墙角，低头看刻度，然后在木板上画下一道线。He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
sceneCN: 这里是「长度」（第 1 个义项：从一端到另一端的量）；句意是他在裁板之前先量了桌子的长度。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、木板、铅笔与墙角。

derivatives.zh: 由 length 加 -y 构成，义为「冗长的；漫长的」
由 length 加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「加长；变长」
由 length 与 wise 复合而成，义为「纵向地；沿长度方向」

senses.title: The measurement from end to end
senses.definition: the distance measured along something from one end to the other
senses.definitionCN: 沿某物从一端量到另一端的距离
senses.example: He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他在裁板之前量了桌子的长度。
senses.why: Old English lengþu was built from lang plus a suffix of abstract nouns, so the word names the quality a thing has by being long.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lengþu 由 lang（长）加抽象名词后缀构成，所以这个词指的就是事物「长」这一性质。

senses.title: The amount of time something lasts
senses.definition: the period during which something continues from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 某件事从开始到结束所持续的时间
senses.example: The length of the film surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的时长让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a line with two ends, so the same word for spatial extent is borrowed to measure how long an event runs.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条有两端的线，于是表示空间延展的同一个词被借来量一件事持续多久。

senses.title: The extent to which something is done
senses.definition: how fully or how far an action, argument or piece of writing is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 行动、论述或文章做到多完整、多深入
senses.example: The report discussed the causes at length.
senses.exampleCN: 报告详细讨论了各种原因。
senses.why: Just as a physical thing has a measurable extent, an argument can be carried to a certain extent, which gives the phrase at length its sense of full treatment.
senses.whyCN: 正如实物有可量的延展，一段论述也能被推进到某个「长度」，于是 at length 就有了「充分论述」的意思。

senses.title: A piece cut from something long
senses.definition: a measured piece of rope, pipe or cloth taken from a longer whole
senses.definitionCN: 从更长的整根绳、管或布上截下来的一段
senses.example: She cut a length of rope to tie the box.
senses.exampleCN: 她截了一段绳子来捆箱子。
senses.why: Once length names a measurable extent, a piece that has exactly that extent can itself be called a length, especially in rope and timber.
senses.whyCN: 既然 length 表示可量的长度，那么恰好具有这个长度的一段东西也就能被称为 a length，绳索与木料尤其如此。

intro.en: Length is the oldest English way of naming the quality of being long, formed from the adjective long with a suffix that builds abstract nouns.
intro.cn: length 是英语里指「长」这一性质最古老的说法，由形容词 long 加上构成抽象名词的后缀而来。

items.en: A reconstructed form dlonghos underlies the family of long words, and the same root appears in Latin longus, which is why the two branches look alike.
items.cn: 重构形式 dlonghos 是这一族「长」词的共同来源，同一词根也出现在拉丁语 longus，因此两条分支看起来相似。

items.en: Old English lang meant long in space and in time, and it could also describe a tall person.
items.cn: 古英语 lang 既指空间上的长，也指时间上的长，还能形容人个子高。

items.en: Adding the abstract suffix -þu to lang produced lengþu, the state or measure of being long.
items.cn: 在 lang 后加抽象名词后缀 -þu 得到 lengþu，即「长」的状态或量。

items.en: Middle English respelled the word with th and dropped the old ending, arriving at forms like lengthe.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写改成 th 并丢掉旧词尾，出现了 lengthe 这样的形式。

items.en: Modern English settled on length, kept lengths as its plural, and extended the sense to duration and to a measured piece.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 length，复数 lengths，并把词义扩展到时长与截下的一段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjectives and verbs built on the same long root; the near-meaning group collects words for measured extent and time span.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「长」词根上的形容词与动词；近义组收表示量度延展与时间跨度的词。

entries.definition: Lasting too long or taking more time than needed.
entries.definitionCN: 持续过久或比需要的更费时的。

entries.definition: To make something longer or to become longer.
entries.definitionCN: 使变长；变长。

entries.definition: The adjective from which length was built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成 length 的那个形容词。

entries.definition: Distance east or west on the earth, from the Latin word for length.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上的东西距离，来自拉丁语中表示「长度」的词。

entries.definition: The space between two points.
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间的空间。

entries.definition: The time during which something continues.
entries.definitionCN: 某事持续的时间。

entries.definition: The degree to which something reaches or is true.
entries.definitionCN: 某物达到的范围或真实程度。

entries.definition: The full distance or period from one end to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一端到另一端的全部距离或时段。

normalIntro.en: The word is the abstract noun of long, and its family keeps returning to measurement in space, measurement in time and the extent of an action.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 long 的抽象名词，同族词反复回到空间上的量、时间上的量，以及行动的推进程度。

normal.en: Length is long turned into a noun: if a thing is long, its length is the measure of that.
normal.cn: length 是把 long 变成名词：一个东西「长」，它的 length 就是这份长的量。

normal.en: The plural is lengths with th kept, not lengthths, so the spelling adds only an s after the th.
normal.cn: 复数是 lengths，th 保留不动，只在 th 后加 s。

normal.en: Lengthen adds -en to length and turns the measure back into an action of making longer.
normal.cn: lengthen 在 length 后加 -en，把「量」又变回「使之变长」的动作。

normal.en: Lengthy adds -y but carries a hint of criticism: more length than the situation needs.
normal.cn: lengthy 加 -y，却带一点批评意味：长度超过了场合所需。

normal.en: At length means two things at once: after a long time, and in full detail.
normal.cn: at length 同时有两个意思：经过很长时间之后，以及详细地。

abstract.en: The same word measures a table, a film and an argument, which shows how readily English maps time and reasoning onto space.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能量桌子、量影片、量论述，说明英语很自然地把时间和论证都投射到空间上。

abstract.en: A measured piece of rope is called a length, so the abstract measure becomes a concrete object when a knife cuts it.
abstract.cn: 截下的一段绳子也叫 a length，于是抽象的量在刀落下时变成了具体的物。

abstract.en: Long is the adjective of desire and length is its measure, but lengthy is the word we use when the desire has gone on too long.
abstract.cn: long 是表示渴望的形容词，length 是它的度量，而 lengthy 用在「拖得太久」的时候。

examples.en: He measured the length of the table before cutting the board.
examples.cn: 他在裁板之前量了桌子的长度。

examples.en: The length of the film surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 这部电影的时长让所有人都感到意外。

examples.en: She cut a length of rope to tie the box.
examples.cn: 她截了一段绳子来捆箱子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「愣是」——这根绳子愣是有三米长；记住 length 是长度。

root: 原始印欧语重构形式 dlonghos（长）→ 古英语 lang → 加抽象后缀 -þu 成 lengþu → 中古英语 lengthe → 现代英语 length；与拉丁语 longus 同出一源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the measure of being long; the senses then apply that measure to time, to how far an action is carried, and to a piece cut to that size.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「长」的量；义项再把这个量用到时间上、用到行动推进的程度上，以及用到恰好截成那么长的一段东西上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tape measure stretched from a corner to the far edge of a board.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷尺从墙角一直拉到木板的另一头。

branches.en: a tape measure lying along a plank
branches.cn: 沿木板铺开的卷尺

branches.en: a clock face marking a two-hour film
branches.cn: 标出一部两小时影片的钟面

branches.en: a report read slowly, page after page
branches.cn: 一页页慢慢读完的报告

branches.en: a coil of rope cut with a knife
branches.cn: 被刀截断的一盘绳

branches.en: a speaker who finally reaches the point
branches.cn: 终于讲到要点的说话人

intro.en: The word joins the adjective long to an Old English suffix for abstract nouns, and the family then adds endings for quality, action and direction.
intro.cn: 这个词把形容词 long 与古英语的抽象名词后缀接在一起，同族词再加上表示性质、动作与方向的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: measuring much from end to end
items.meaningCN: 从一端到另一端很长的

definition_zh: 透镜；镜片；晶状体；镜头；视角
definition_en: a curved piece of glass or plastic that bends light, the matching part of the eye, the glass element of a camera, and a way of looking at a subject
core_image: 一枚弧形玻璃片把远处的灯光收成一个小亮点
scene: 摄影师的桌上，一枚弧形玻璃片被布擦得发亮，远处的灯在它里面缩成一点。He cleaned the lens before shooting the portrait.
sceneCN: 这里是「镜头」（第 3 个义项：相机上那片可更换的玻璃）；句意是他在拍人像之前先擦净了镜头。图中可辨识物件：擦镜布、弧形玻璃片、桌上的相机。

pos.zh: 透镜；镜片；晶状体；镜头；视角

derivatives.zh: 由 lens 与 man 复合而成，义为「摄影师；镜头工作者」
由 lens 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无镜片的」
源自拉丁语小词 lenticula，义为「透镜状的；小扁豆形的」

senses.title: A curved piece of glass that bends light
senses.definition: a shaped piece of glass or plastic used to focus or spread light in an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 仪器中用来聚光或散光的成形玻璃片或塑料片
senses.example: The microscope needs a stronger lens to show the cells clearly.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜需要更强的镜片才能把细胞看清。
senses.why: The word starts as the name of a lentil, because a biconvex piece of glass has the same plump oval shape as the seed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初只是「小扁豆」的名字，因为双凸的玻璃片和那颗种子一样呈饱满的椭圆。

senses.title: The light-focusing part of the eye
senses.definition: the small clear structure inside the eye that focuses images on the retina
senses.definitionCN: 眼球内把影像聚焦到视网膜上的透明小结构
senses.example: The lens of the eye focuses light onto the retina.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛的晶状体把光聚焦到视网膜上。
senses.why: Once lens names any shaped body that focuses light, the eye's own focusing body takes the same name by analogy of function.
senses.whyCN: 既然 lens 能指任何聚光的成形体，眼睛自带的聚光结构就按功能类比得到了同一个名字。

senses.title: The glass element of a camera
senses.definition: the glass unit fitted to a camera, often one of several that can be exchanged
senses.definitionCN: 装在相机上的玻璃组件，常为可更换的若干支之一
senses.example: He cleaned the lens before shooting the portrait.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拍人像之前先擦净了镜头。
senses.why: A camera is built around the same bending of light that a single lens performs, and the whole glass assembly simply borrows the part's name.
senses.whyCN: 相机正是围绕单片镜片所做的同一件弯光之事造出来的，于是整组玻璃组件干脆沿用了零件的名字。

senses.title: A way of looking at a subject
senses.definition: a particular standpoint that shapes how a subject is understood
senses.definitionCN: 决定人们如何理解某个主题的特定立场
senses.example: Viewed through the lens of history, the quarrel looks small.
senses.exampleCN: 从历史的视角看，那场争吵显得微不足道。
senses.why: A lens decides what enters the eye and how it is bent, so the word naturally becomes a metaphor for whatever selects and shapes our view.
senses.whyCN: 镜片决定什么进入眼睛、又如何被弯曲，于是这个词很自然地成了比喻，指那些筛选并塑造视野的东西。

intro.en: Lens is Latin for lentil; the optical sense was borrowed by seventeenth-century writers because a biconvex glass looked like the seed.
intro.cn: lens 在拉丁语里就是「小扁豆」；十七世纪的学者借它来指光学镜片，因为双凸玻璃的形状像那颗种子。

items.en: Lens, with the stem lent-, named the lentil, the small flat seed of a plant in the pea family.
items.cn: lens（词干 lent-）指小扁豆，即豆科植物那种小而扁的种子。

items.en: The diminutive lenticula named a small lentil and later supplied English lentil and the adjective lenticular.
items.cn: 小词形式 lenticula 指一颗小扁豆，后来为英语提供了 lentil 与形容词 lenticular。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers of optics borrowed lens for a curved piece of glass, since a biconvex shape resembles a lentil.
items.cn: 十七世纪的光学作者借 lens 指弧形玻璃片，因为双凸形状与扁豆相似。

items.en: English took lens as a technical term of microscopy and astronomy, where curved glass was newly powerful.
items.cn: 英语把 lens 当作显微镜与天文学的技术术语引入，那时弧形玻璃刚刚显示出威力。

items.en: Modern English extended lens to the eye's own focusing body, to camera optics and to any selective point of view.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lens 扩展到眼睛自带的聚焦结构、相机光学，以及任何有筛选作用的视角。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the seed word behind the name and the forms built on it; the near-meaning group collects other optical parts that bend or split light.
note.cn: 形近组收这个名字背后的「种子」词及其派生形式；近义组收其他弯曲或分解光线的光学部件。

entries.definition: The small flat seed that gave the lens its name.
entries.definitionCN: 给透镜命名的这种小而扁的种子。

entries.definition: Shaped like a lentil or a lens.
entries.definitionCN: 形状像扁豆或透镜的。

entries.definition: A photographer or cameraman, especially in news work.
entries.definitionCN: 摄影师或摄影记者。

entries.definition: Made or working without a lens.
entries.definitionCN: 无镜片的；不用镜片工作的。

entries.definition: The hard transparent material that lenses are usually made from.
entries.definitionCN: 制作镜片常用的坚硬透明材料。

entries.definition: A shaped piece of glass that splits light into colours.
entries.definitionCN: 把光分解成多种颜色的成形玻璃。

entries.definition: A lens or device that makes small things look bigger.
entries.definitionCN: 使小东西看起来更大的镜片或装置。

entries.definition: The lens or lens group you look through in an instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器上供眼睛观看的那片或那组镜片。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin for a seed, and the whole optical family keeps returning to that plump oval shape and to the bending of light.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里是一颗种子，整个光学词族反复回到那个饱满的椭圆形状与弯折的光线。

normal.en: Latin lens means lentil, so the glass was named for its shape rather than for its function.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lens 意为扁豆，所以这片玻璃是因形状得名，而不是因功能得名。

normal.en: Lentil and lens share one root: the seed and the glass are the same oval seen at different sizes.
normal.cn: lentil 与 lens 同根：种子与玻璃是同一个椭圆在不同尺度上的样子。

normal.en: Lenticular adds -ar to the Latin diminutive and means shaped like a lentil or a lens.
normal.cn: lenticular 在拉丁小词后加 -ar，意为「扁豆状或透镜状的」。

normal.en: Lensless adds -less: an instrument without that curved piece cannot focus anything.
normal.cn: lensless 加 -less：少了那片弧形玻璃，仪器就什么也聚不了。

normal.en: Through the lens of is the phrase to keep: it turns an optical part into a way of judging.
normal.cn: 要记住 through the lens of 这个说法：它把一片光学零件变成了一种评判方式。

abstract.en: A seed, a glass, an eye and a standpoint all answer to one word, because each of them selects and focuses what comes through.
abstract.cn: 种子、玻璃、眼睛与立场都由同一个词承担，因为它们都在筛选并聚焦穿过自己之物。

abstract.en: The history of lens shows how a name for shape can quietly become a name for power: the power to decide what is seen.
abstract.cn: lens 的历史说明，一个形状之名可以悄悄变成能力之名：决定什么能被看见的能力。

abstract.en: Calling a view a lens reminds us that no standpoint is perfectly clear glass; every one bends what it shows.
abstract.cn: 把视角称作 lens，提醒人没有任何立场是毫无偏折的玻璃，每一种都会弯折它所呈现的东西。

examples.en: The microscope needs a stronger lens to show the cells clearly.
examples.cn: 显微镜需要更强的镜片才能把细胞看清。

examples.en: The lens of the eye focuses light onto the retina.
examples.cn: 眼睛的晶状体把光聚焦到视网膜上。

examples.en: Viewed through the lens of history, the quarrel looks small.
examples.cn: 从历史的视角看，那场争吵显得微不足道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「棱子」——镜片边缘像棱子；记住 lens 是透镜、镜片。

root: 拉丁语 lens（小扁豆，词干 lent-）→ 十七世纪借作光学名词，因双凸镜片形似扁豆 → 现代英语扩展至晶状体、相机镜头与看待事物的视角。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a lentil-shaped glass that bends light; the senses then move to the eye's own focusing body, the camera's glass unit, and the metaphor of a selective standpoint.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是形似扁豆、弯折光线的玻璃；义项由此转到眼睛自带的聚焦结构、相机的玻璃组件，以及「有筛选作用的立场」这一比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small curved glass disc on a cloth, gathering a distant lamp into one bright point.
core.cn: 核心意象：布上一枚小小的弧形玻璃片，把远处的灯收成一个亮点。

branches.en: a glass disc bending a beam onto a slide
branches.cn: 把光束弯到载玻片上的玻璃片

branches.en: a pupil widening in a dim room
branches.cn: 暗房里慢慢张开的瞳孔

branches.en: a photographer wiping the front glass
branches.cn: 摄影师擦拭最前那片玻璃

branches.en: a historian reframing an old quarrel
branches.cn: 重新框定旧日争吵的历史学家

branches.en: a documentary filmed from one angle
branches.cn: 只从一个角度拍摄的纪录片

intro.en: The word is a Latin seed name, its diminutive and a Latin suffix, and English then builds the optical compounds and negatives that surround it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「种子」名、它的小词形式与一个拉丁后缀构成，英语再围绕它造出光学复合词与否定义。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 水平高度；水位；水平；程度；楼层；平的；使平坦；夷平
definition_en: the height of something measured from the ground, a standard or amount used for comparison, a floor of a building, or to make a surface flat
core_image: 玻璃管里的气泡停在两条刻线之间，管身与桌面平行
scene: 雨后的池塘退了水，孩子们站在石阶上量了量，水只到膝盖。The water level had dropped to the children's knees.
sceneCN: 这里是「水位、水平高度」（第 1 个义项：离地量出的高度）；句意为水位已经降到孩子们的膝盖那么低。图中可辨识物件：石阶、浅浅的池水、卷起的裤脚。

pos.zh: 水平高度；水位；水平；程度；楼层

derivatives.zh: 由 level 加 -er 构成，义为「把东西弄平的人或工具；主张人人平等的人」
由 level 加 -ing 构成，义为「平整；拉平」
由 level 与 headed 复合，义为「头脑冷静的；不慌不乱的」

senses.title: The height of something above the ground
senses.definition: the height of a surface or mass, measured from the ground or from a fixed line
senses.definitionCN: 某表面或物体相对地面，或相对某条固定基准线的高度
senses.example: The water level had dropped to the children's knees.
senses.exampleCN: 水位已经降到孩子们的膝盖那么低。
senses.why: The Latin libella was a plumb line and a small water tube used on building sites; measuring upward from a trusted flat line is exactly the job of that instrument, so the first sense is a measured height.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 libella 是铅垂线和小水器，在工地上专门用来从一条可信的平线往上量；所以这个词最早的义项就是量出来的高度。

senses.title: A standard or amount used for comparison
senses.definition: the amount, rank or quality of something, especially when set beside other things
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的数量、等级或质量，尤指与其他事物并排比较时
senses.example: Her reading level is far above her age.
senses.exampleCN: 她的阅读水平远远超过她的年龄。
senses.why: Once a flat line is trusted, it can serve as a reference for anything else; the word then leaves space and becomes a scale on which people and results are placed.
senses.whyCN: 一条平线一旦可信，就能当作其他东西的参照；于是这个词离开空间，变成一把给人或成果定位的尺子。

senses.title: One floor of a building
senses.definition: one of the floors or storeys of a building, counted upward from the ground
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物中的一层，从地面往上计数
senses.example: The library takes up the third level of the building.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆占了这栋楼的第三层。
senses.why: A tall building is a stack of flat horizontal slices, and every slice rests at one height; English names that slice with the same word it uses for the height itself.
senses.whyCN: 高楼是一层层水平切片叠起来的，每一片都停在一个高度；英语就用表示「高度」的同一个词来命名这一片。

senses.title: Flat and even, with no part higher than another
senses.definition: having a surface that is flat and even, with no part standing above the rest
senses.definitionCN: 表面平直，没有一处高过其余部分
senses.example: The floor must be level before the tiles go down.
senses.exampleCN: 铺地砖之前地面必须是平的。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the literal picture: the surface a plumb line or a water tube would approve of, with nothing sticking up anywhere.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留最字面的画面：那是铅垂线或水管量过也挑不出毛病、任何地方都没有突起的面。

senses.title: To make a surface flat or knock a building down
senses.definition: to make something flat and even, or to bring a building down until it meets the ground
senses.definitionCN: 把某物弄平，或把建筑物拆到与地面齐平
senses.example: Workers levelled the old wall to make room for the park.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把旧墙推平，为公园腾出地方。
senses.why: If evenness is the goal, the verb is the labour of reaching it; tearing a building down leaves the ground at a single height, so demolition joins the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然「平」是要达到的状态，动词就是达到它的那番劳作；把楼拆掉之后地面只剩一个高度，于是拆除也归进同一个词。

intro.en: Level comes from a Latin word for a balance, shrunk into the name of a small measuring instrument, then reshaped by French before English widened it.
intro.cn: level 来自拉丁语中表示「天平」的词，先缩成一件小测量器具的名字，又经法语改写，最后被英语大幅扩展。

items.en: Libra meant a balance or a pair of scales, and it also named a Roman unit of weight.
items.cn: libra 意为天平、秤，同时也指罗马的一种重量单位。

items.en: A libella was a small balance; on a building site it meant a plumb line or a little water tube for testing whether a surface was even.
items.cn: libella 是小天平；在工地上它指铅垂线或测平的小水器，用来检验一个面是否平直。

items.en: Old French kept the word as livel, still tied to the instrument and to the idea of an even surface.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 livel，仍与那件器具以及「表面平直」的观念相连。

items.en: Middle English level first names the instrument for testing flatness, then the flat surface itself.
items.cn: 中古英语的 level 先指检验平直的器具，随后指平直的面本身。

items.en: Modern English extends level to height above the ground, standards of achievement, floors of buildings, and the act of flattening.
items.cn: 现代英语把 level 扩展到离地高度、成就水平、楼房层数，以及弄平的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of weighing and balancing; the near-meaning group gathers words for height, rank and flatness.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中「称量、平衡」的词干展开；近义组收表示高度、等级与平坦的词。

entries.definition: A balance or pair of scales in Latin, and the name of the zodiac sign of the scales.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的天平或秤，也是黄道十二宫天秤座的名字。

entries.definition: The small balance that became the plumb line and water level of builders.
entries.definitionCN: 由「天平」缩成的小词，后来成为工匠的铅垂线与水平器。

entries.definition: A state of balance, built on the Latin word for a pair of scales.
entries.definitionCN: 平衡状态，建立在拉丁语「天平」一词之上。

entries.definition: Carefully weighed in the mind, from a Latin verb meaning to weigh.
entries.definitionCN: 经过仔细权衡的，来自意为「称量」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The distance from the ground upward.
entries.definitionCN: 从地面往上的距离；高度。

entries.definition: A level of quality used as a measure.
entries.definitionCN: 用作衡量标准的质量水准。

entries.definition: A floor of a building, the usual British word.
entries.definitionCN: 楼房的层，英式常用说法。

entries.definition: Smooth and even, with no bumps or slopes.
entries.definitionCN: 平滑而没有突起或倾斜的。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a little balance used to test a flat surface, and its family keeps returning to evenness and measurement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一件用来检验平面小天平，同族词反复回到「平」与「量」。

normal.en: Libra is Latin for a balance, and libella is its small form, so level starts life as a tool for judging whether a surface is even.
normal.cn: libra 是拉丁语的「天平」，libella 是它的小称，所以 level 最初是一件判断表面平不平的工具。

normal.en: A plumb line hangs straight down, and a surface is level when that line meets it squarely.
normal.cn: 铅垂线笔直垂下，当一个面与它正好垂直相交时，那个面就是平的。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the l: levelled and levelling; American spelling keeps one l.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，写作 levelled 与 levelling；美式只写一个 l。

normal.en: Sea level is the even reference line from which heights on land are measured.
normal.cn: 海平面就是那条水平的基准线，陆地上的高度都从它量起。

normal.en: To level a building is to take away every height that stood above the ground.
normal.cn: 把一栋楼 level 掉，就是把高过地面的每一寸都去掉。

abstract.en: One word covering height, rank, floor and flattening suggests English sees them all as positions on a single even line.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示高度、等级、楼层和弄平，说明英语把它们都看成同一条平线上的位置。

abstract.en: Fairness borrows the same picture: a level playing field gives nobody a slope to run down.
abstract.cn: 公平也借用了同一幅画面：平坦的球场不会给任何人一个下坡。

abstract.en: Checking a surface with a bubble is a small act of trusting gravity to tell the truth.
abstract.cn: 用气泡检验一个面，是让重力说真话的一件小事。

examples.en: The water level had dropped to the children's knees.
examples.cn: 水位已经降到孩子们的膝盖那么低。

examples.en: The floor must be level before the tiles go down.
examples.cn: 铺地砖之前地面必须是平的。

examples.en: Workers levelled the old wall to make room for the park.
examples.cn: 工人们把旧墙推平，为公园腾出地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来我这儿」——干活前先看看地面平不平；level 就是水平、弄平。

root: 拉丁语 libra（天平、秤）的指小形式 libella（小天平、铅垂线），经古法语 livel 进入英语；同族词多与称量、平直有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line that sits even with the ground; from it flow measured height, rank on a scale, stacked floors, and the adjective and verb of flatness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一条与地面齐平的线；由此分出量出的高度、尺度上的等级、叠起的楼层，以及表示「平」的形容词和动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bubble resting between two marks in a glass tube laid across a board.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃管横放在木板上，管里的气泡停在两道刻线之间。

branches.en: a river gauge recording how high the water stands
branches.cn: 记录水位高低的河尺

branches.en: a bubble settling in the middle of a tube
branches.cn: 气泡停在管子中央

branches.en: a chart ranking readers by reading age
branches.cn: 按阅读年龄给读者分级的图表

branches.en: a lift stopping at a numbered floor
branches.cn: 停在某一层的电梯

branches.en: a wall coming down until the ground is clear
branches.cn: 墙被推倒，直到地面清空

intro.en: A Latin balance, its small form, a French reshaping and two English suffixes carry this word from instrument to height, rank and floor.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「天平」、它的指小形式、一次法语改写和两个英语后缀，把这个词从器具一路带到高度、等级与楼层。

latinIntro.en: Libra and its small form libella belong to the Latin vocabulary of weighing and measuring, and both are recorded words.
latinIntro.cn: libra 与它的指小形式 libella 都属于拉丁语称量与测量的词汇，两者都是有记录的实词。

items.meaningCN: 把东西弄平的人；平等主义者

definition_zh: 负债；责任；不利条件
definition_en: a legal or financial obligation to pay or do something; something that causes risk or difficulty
core_image: 一个人的脚上拴着一块大铁球，铁球上刻着「欠债必须还」，旁边摆着一份写着 liability 的表格
scene: 公司财务报表的右侧列着各种要付的钱：应付账款、长期借款、应计费用。Every liability on the balance sheet must be matched against an asset.
sceneCN: 这里 liability 指「公司负债」（第 2 个义项：公司财务上应支付的债务）；句意为资产负债表上总负债首次超过了总资产。图中可辨识物件：资产负债表、铁球、欠债数字。

pos.zh: 负债（可数/不可数）；责任（可数）

derivatives.zh: 有责任的；易受的
联络（同拉丁词根但义不同）
责任保险
对……有责任的

senses.title: legal responsibility
senses.definition: a legal obligation to do or pay something
senses.definitionCN: 法律上做某事或付钱的义务
senses.example: The company denied all liability for the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 公司否认对事故负有任何法律责任。
senses.why: liable 'legally bound' + -ity makes the noun of the obligation.
senses.whyCN: liable「法律上有约束力的」+ -ity 就是这种义务的名词。

senses.title: financial debt or obligation
senses.definition: an amount owed in a company's or person's balance sheet
senses.definitionCN: 公司或个人资产负债表上所欠的金额
senses.example: Mortgages are long-term liabilities for households.
senses.exampleCN: 房贷是家庭的长期负债。
senses.why: A financial debt is a liability, something that binds you to pay.
senses.whyCN: 一笔财务债务就是 liability，绑着你去付钱。

senses.title: something that makes you liable
senses.definition: a person or thing that causes risk or exposure
senses.definitionCN: 带来风险或暴露的人或事
senses.example: His reckless driving made him a liability to the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他鲁莽的驾驶让他成了车队的负担。
senses.why: Something that can make you bound to pay is itself a liability.
senses.whyCN: 任何能让你变得要出钱的东西本身就是 liability。

senses.title: tax or other duty
senses.definition: an amount due to a government or authority
senses.definitionCN: 欠政府或当局的金额
senses.example: Tax liabilities rise as profits grow.
senses.exampleCN: 利润增加，应纳税额也跟着上涨。
senses.why: Any amount you are bound to pay is a liability.
senses.whyCN: 任何你必须付的金额都是 liability。

senses.title: limited liability
senses.definition: a legal structure where owners are only responsible for their investment
senses.definitionCN: 所有者仅对其投资负责的法律结构
senses.example: A limited liability company protects personal savings.
senses.exampleCN: 有限责任公司保护了个人的储蓄。
senses.why: The concept of liability is narrowed to protect owners.
senses.whyCN: liability 的概念被收窄来保护所有者。

senses.title: professional liability
senses.definition: legal responsibility of a professional for errors in work
senses.definitionCN: 专业人士对其工作失误的法律责任
senses.example: Doctors buy liability insurance for malpractice claims.
senses.exampleCN: 医生买职业责任险来应对医疗事故索赔。
senses.why: Professionals are bound to their clients for mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 专业人士对其客户的失误有约束力。

senses.title: contractual obligation
senses.definition: an obligation written into a contract between parties
senses.definitionCN: 合同中写明的各方之间的义务
senses.example: The liability to deliver expired when the contract terminated.
senses.exampleCN: 合同终止时，交货义务也过期了。
senses.why: Contracts create binding duties, which are liabilities.
senses.whyCN: 合同创造了有约束力的责任，就是 liabilities。

senses.title: environmental liability
senses.definition: legal obligation to clean up pollution or pay for harm
senses.definitionCN: 清理污染或赔偿损害的法律义务
senses.example: The old factory faces environmental liabilities from decades of waste.
senses.exampleCN: 老工厂因几十年的废弃物面临环境责任。
senses.why: A newer application of the general 'bound to pay' sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是「必须付钱」这个一般义的一个新应用。

intro.en: Liability comes from liable, which comes from Old French lier 'to bind'. Liability is the quality of being bound.
intro.cn: liability 来自 liable，后者来自古法语 lier「绑缚」。liability 就是「被绑着」的状态。

items.en: Latin ligare meant 'to bind'; it gave rise to liare, the Vulgar Latin for 'to bind, tie'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 意为「绑缚」，它产生了通俗拉丁语 liare「绑、系」。

items.en: Old French lier 'to bind, tie' came from Vulgar Latin liare.
items.cn: 古法语 lier「绑、系」来自通俗拉丁语 liare。

items.en: Middle English liabill meant 'legally bound, answerable'; it came from Old French lier.
items.cn: 中古英语 liabill 意为「法律上有约束力的、应负责的」，来自古法语 lier。

items.en: The suffix -ity (Latin -itas via French) turns the adjective liable into the noun liability.
items.cn: 后缀 -ity（拉丁语 -itas 经法语）把形容词 liable 变成名词 liability。

items.en: The balance-sheet sense 'debts owed' developed by the 17th century, as a debt binds you.
items.cn: 资产负债表上的「所欠债务」义在 17 世纪形成，因为债务就是绑着你的东西。

items.en: Etymology solid; ligare is well attested in classical Latin.
items.cn: 词源可靠；ligare 在古典拉丁语中有充分文献。

note.en: Look-alikes share the lig- bind root; near meanings are obligations or debts.
note.cn: 形近共享 lig-「绑」词根；近义是义务或债务。

entries.definition: Legally bound or responsible; liability is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上有约束力的或应负责的；liability 是它的名词。

entries.definition: A band of tissue that binds bones together.
entries.definitionCN: 把骨头绑在一起的一条组织。

entries.definition: To bind morally or legally; same lig- root.
entries.definitionCN: 在道德或法律上约束；同 lig- 词根。

entries.definition: To communicate and coordinate; from the same lier 'to bind'.
entries.definitionCN: 沟通协调；来自同一个 lier「绑」。

entries.definition: A specific sum owed; liability is broader and includes non-monetary obligations too.
entries.definitionCN: 所欠的一笔具体金额；liability 更宽，也包括非金钱义务。

entries.definition: A duty one is bound to perform; liability is specifically legal/financial.
entries.definitionCN: 被约束必须履行的义务；liability 特指法律/财务上的。

entries.definition: A general duty to act, not necessarily legal or financial.
entries.definitionCN: 一般性的行动义务，不一定是法律或财务的。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实配对。

normal.en: Latin ligare 'to bind' → Old French lier → liable → liability.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ligare「绑缚」→ 古法语 lier → liable → liability。

normal.en: liable = bound; liability = the state of being bound.
normal.cn: liable = 被绑住的；liability = 被绑住的状态。

normal.en: Balance sheet: assets = what you own, liabilities = what you owe.
normal.cn: 资产负债表：assets = 你拥有的，liabilities = 你欠下的。

abstract.en: Picture a man chained to a pile of coins that grows bigger every month.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人被铁链拴在一堆每个月都在长大的硬币上。

abstract.en: Picture Latin ligare: ropes tying you to what you owe.
abstract.cn: 想象拉丁语 ligare：绳子把你绑在你欠的东西上。

abstract.en: Picture a company's balance sheet as a seesaw: assets on one side, liabilities on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象公司的资产负债表是一架跷跷板：一边是资产，一边是负债。

examples.en: The startup took on significant liabilities to fund its rapid expansion.
examples.cn: 那家初创公司为快速扩张承担了大量负债。

examples.en: Owners of a limited liability company are not personally on the hook for its debts.
examples.cn: 有限责任公司的所有者不亲自替公司的债务背锅。

examples.en: The manufacturer faces product-liability claims from thousands of injured consumers.
examples.cn: 该制造商面临数千名受伤消费者的产品责任索赔。

definition_zh: 自由；自由权；擅自；获准行动的范围
definition_en: freedom to live and act as one chooses, especially as a condition protected by law or constitution
core_image: 一根被砸断的锁链落在石阶上，锁孔里还插着半截钥匙，人已经走远
scene: 城邦的公民在广场上宣读宪章，声称任何人不得未经审判而被拘押。Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
sceneCN: 这里指「受法律保障、不受任意拘押的个人自由」，对应第 1 个义项：法律保护的、免于任意逮捕的自由；句意为公民宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人。画面要点：广场、宪章、砸断的锁链。

pos.zh: 自由；自由权（不可数；表示各项具体自由时可用复数）

collocations.zh: 获准的；自由的；有空闲的

derivatives.zh: 自由的；宽容的；自由主义的（拉丁语中表示「自由人的、宽厚的」形容词经法语传入，语义由身份转向宽宏与开明）
解放；释放（表示「自由的」词根加动词后缀，指使某人脱离束缚）
解放；释放（动词加表行为的名词后缀，指使脱离束缚的过程）
自由意志论者（表示「自由」的名词加表主张或从事者的后缀，指主张个人自由最大化的人）

senses.title: Protection from arbitrary detention
senses.titleCN: 免于任意拘押的个人自由
senses.definition: the condition of a person who cannot be arrested or held except by lawful procedure
senses.definitionCN: 除依法定程序外不得被逮捕或拘押的个人状态
senses.example: Citizens in the square read out the charter declaring that no one should be detained without trial, a guarantee of personal liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 公民在广场宣读宪章，宣布未经审判不得拘押任何人，这是对个人自由的保障。
senses.why: In Roman law the free person's body could not be seized at will, so liberty begins as a legal status rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 在罗马法中，自由人的身体不能被随意捉拿，因此「自由」一开始是一种法律身份，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: Self-government of a community
senses.definition: the condition of a city or people that makes its own laws instead of receiving them from a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 城市或民族自行立法、而不是从统治者那里接受法律的状态
senses.example: The city kept its liberties against the duke for two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城邦两代人以来一直保有对抗公爵的自由权。
senses.why: Medieval towns bought charters that listed their liberties, so the word came to name a body's collective self-rule.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪城镇买下特许状，状上逐条列出它们的自由权，于是这个词也命名一个群体的自治。

senses.title: Specific rights protected by law
senses.titleCN: 法律保护的各项具体自由权
senses.definition: the several freedoms, such as speech, worship and assembly, that a constitution or statute guarantees
senses.definitionCN: 宪法或法律所保障的若干项自由，如言论、礼拜与集会
senses.example: The bill lists the liberties that the state may not remove.
senses.exampleCN: 权利法案列出了国家不得取消的各项自由。
senses.why: The abstract condition becomes countable when each guarantee is written down separately, which is why the plural is so common in legal texts.
senses.whyCN: 当每一项保障被分别写下来，抽象状态就变得可数，这就是复数形式在法律文本中如此常见的原因。

senses.title: Overstepping what is allowed
senses.definition: the act of acting beyond one's permitted scope, especially in a way that is presumptuous
senses.definitionCN: 超出自己被允许的范围行事，尤指冒失无礼地这样做
senses.example: The visitor took liberties with the archive and rearranged the files.
senses.exampleCN: 那位访客擅自摆弄档案，把文件重新排列了。
senses.why: A granted latitude can be used too far, so the same noun turns ironic and names the abuse of a permission.
senses.whyCN: 获准的余地可能被用过了头，于是同一个名词转为反讽，命名对许可的滥用。

senses.title: Being permitted or free to act
senses.definition: the state of being allowed to do something, or of being free from obligation at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 获准做某事、或在某一时刻没有义务在身的状态
senses.example: You are at liberty to inspect the records yourself.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以自行查阅这些记录。
senses.why: The phrase 'at liberty' keeps the old legal sense of a person not under restraint, and from it comes the polite formula for permission.
senses.whyCN: 「处于自由状态」这一短语保留了「人未受拘束」的旧法律义，礼貌的许可说法正是从这里来的。

senses.title: Freedom of conscience and worship
senses.definition: the right to hold and practise a faith without state pressure
senses.definitionCN: 不受国家压力地持有并实践信仰的权利
senses.example: Religious liberty was the first liberty to be argued for in print.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教自由是最早被以印刷文字论证的自由。
senses.why: Where the state and the church were the same body, the demand to worship otherwise was the sharpest test of a protected sphere.
senses.whyCN: 当国家与教会合为一体，要求以别的方式礼拜，就成了对「受保护领域」最尖锐的检验。

senses.title: Freedom of the will
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that a person can choose without being wholly determined by prior causes
senses.definitionCN: 人能够作出选择、而不完全被先在原因所决定的哲学主张
senses.example: The essay asks whether liberty of the will survives a strict causal account.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章追问，在严格的决定论解释下，意志自由是否还能成立。
senses.why: Once legal restraint is removed, the remaining question is whether anything else restrains the will, and the word follows the question inward.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法律约束被移除，剩下的问题就是是否有别的东西在约束意志，这个词便随问题向内走。

senses.title: The range of a granted freedom
senses.definition: the extent of a place or body of knowledge that a person is allowed to use
senses.definitionCN: 一个人被允许使用的场所或知识范围
senses.example: The scholar was given the liberty of the whole collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者获准自由使用全部藏书。
senses.why: To have the liberty of a place is an old civic formula: not ownership, but the permitted run of it.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有某地的自由」是一个古老的市民说法：不是所有权，而是被允许在其中往来。

intro.en: Liberty comes from Latin libertas, the condition of a free person, built on liber 'free'. The deeper origin of liber is uncertain. English took the word through Old French, and its plural came to mean specific chartered privileges.
intro.cn: liberty 出自拉丁语 libertas，指自由人的身份，建立在 liber「自由的」之上。liber 的更深来源不确定。英语经古法语吸收此词，其复数后来指特许状上具体列明的特权。

items.en: Liber meant 'free, not a slave' and could also describe a person of noble or generous status. Its own origin is uncertain; a connection with a root meaning 'to grow' has been suggested but not established.
items.cn: liber 意为「自由的、非奴隶的」，也可形容出身高贵或气度宽厚的人。它本身的来源不确定；有人提出它与意为「生长」的词根相关，但未获确立。

items.en: Libertas named the condition of a free person and, in Roman public life, the status that law protected against arbitrary seizure.
items.cn: libertas 指自由人的身份；在罗马公共生活中，它指法律保护、免于任意捉拿的身份。

items.en: Old French liberte carried the noun into English, at first in religious and civic contexts rather than in philosophy.
items.cn: 古法语 liberte 把这个名词带入英语，最初用于宗教与市民语境，而不是哲学。

items.en: Towns and guilds listed their liberties in charters, and the plural became a name for specific privileges held by a body.
items.cn: 城镇与行会在特许状中逐条列出自己的自由权，其复数形式于是成为某个群体所持具体特权的名称。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the singular named a general political condition, and documents began to speak of civil liberty. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，单数形式指一般的政治状态，文书开始谈论公民自由。年代为约数。

items.en: The same noun was applied to the will, producing the long debate over liberty of the will that continues in philosophy.
items.cn: 同一个名词被用到意志上，产生了关于意志自由的长期争论，这一争论在哲学中延续至今。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective or looks deceptively close to it, including one word whose Latin source is a different noun altogether; the second group gives near alternatives.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个拉丁形容词构成或与它形近得容易误认，其中还有一个词的拉丁来源是另一个名词；第二组是近义替代。

entries.definition: Generous or open-minded, and in politics favourable to reform; it began as 'of a free person' and moved toward generosity of attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 宽厚的、开明的，政治上倾向改革；它起初意为「自由人的」，后来转向态度上的宽宏。

entries.definition: To set a person or place free from control; it names the act that produces liberty rather than the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 使人或地方脱离控制；它命名产生自由的动作，而不是状态。

entries.definition: A place where books are kept; its Latin source is a word for a book or the bark used for writing, not the adjective for freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 藏书之所；它的拉丁来源是表示「书」或书写用树皮的词，而不是表示自由的形容词。

entries.definition: A published false statement that harms a reputation; it comes from a small Latin book or booklet, with no link to freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表的、损害名誉的不实陈述；它出自拉丁语中表示小册子的词，与自由无关。

entries.definition: The general condition of not being bound; it covers body, will and speech, while liberty more often names a legally protected status.
entries.definitionCN: 不受束缚的一般状态；它覆盖身体、意志与言论，而本词更常指受法律保护的身份。

entries.definition: The right of a person or region to govern itself; it stresses who makes the rules rather than what is forbidden.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或地区自行治理的权利；它强调由谁制定规则，而不是禁止什么。

entries.definition: The state of not being controlled or supported by another; it is common for nations and for self-supporting people.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制或供养的状态；常用于国家与自食其力的人。

entries.definition: An official permission to do something; it is narrower than liberty because it is granted case by case and can be revoked.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方许可；它比自由窄，因为逐案授予且可被撤回。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for a free person, real derived words and real legal formulas, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示自由人的形容词、真实派生词与真实法律套语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The core is a legal status: a free body that cannot be seized at will.
normal.cn: 核心是一种法律身份：一具不能被随意捉拿的自由身体。

normal.en: The family runs liberal, liberate, liberation and libertarian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括宽厚的、解放、解放过程与自由意志论者。

normal.en: Medieval towns kept their liberties in written charters, which is why the plural means specific privileges.
normal.cn: 中世纪城镇把自由权写进特许状，所以复数形式指具体特权。

normal.en: The phrase at liberty means both free from restraint and free to act.
normal.cn: 「处于自由状态」这一说法既指不受拘束，也指可以行动。

normal.en: Taking liberties is the ironic side: using a permission further than it was given.
normal.cn: 「擅自」是这个词的反讽一面：把许可用得比给予的更远。

abstract.en: Picture a broken chain on a step with the key still in the lock, and the person already out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象石阶上一根断链，钥匙还插在锁里，人已经走远。

abstract.en: Picture a charter rolled open on a town table, each paragraph a named freedom.
abstract.cn: 想象城镇桌上一卷摊开的特许状，每一段都是一项有名字的自由。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked permission that opens only when the right name is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着「许可」的门，只有说出正确的名分才会打开。

examples.en: The court held that the detention violated his liberty.
examples.cn: 法院认定这次拘押侵犯了他的自由。

examples.en: You are at liberty to leave whenever you wish.
examples.cn: 你随时都可以离开。

examples.en: The reporter took liberties with the quotation and changed its sense.
examples.cn: 那名记者擅自改动引文，改变了它的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离不体」——身体离开束缚，就不必再贴着锁链过日子；自由就是能走开的那一步。

root: 拉丁语 liber「自由的、非奴隶的」→ libertas「自由人的身份」→ 经古法语 liberte 进入英语。liber 的更深来源不确定，与意为「生长」的词根相关的说法属假说；同族的 liberalis 意为「自由人的、宽厚的」，是另一条语义支线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings start from a free body that the law may not seize. From that status come self-rule for a community, the list of named guarantees, the permission formula, the ironic overstepping of permission, the freedom of worship, the philosophical liberty of the will, and the old civic right to move through a place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一具法律不得随意捉拿的自由身体开始。从这个身份分出共同体的自治、逐条列名的保障、许可的说法、对许可的反讽式越界、信仰的自由、哲学上的意志自由，以及古老的、可在某地往来的市民权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain broken at the link, with the key still turning in the lock.
core.cn: 核心意象：链环被砸断的锁链，钥匙还在锁里转动。

branches.en: UNBOUND BODY: protection from arbitrary arrest, and the polite formula that a person is free to act.
branches.cn: 不受束缚的身体：免于任意逮捕，以及「可以自由行动」的礼貌说法。

branches.en: SELF-RULE: a town or people that makes its own law.
branches.cn: 自治：自行立法的城镇或民族。

branches.en: NAMED GUARANTEES: the several liberties written in a charter, and the permitted run of a place.
branches.cn: 列名的保障：写进特许状的各项自由，以及在某地获准走动的范围。

branches.en: OVERSTEPPING: the same permission used beyond what was granted.
branches.cn: 越界：同一份许可被用得超出所给予的范围。

branches.en: CONSCIENCE AND WILL: worship without pressure, and the inner question of whether the will is determined.
branches.cn: 良心与意志：不受压力的礼拜，以及意志是否被决定的内在问题。

intro.en: The whole family rests on one Latin adjective for a free person, with noun, verb and agent endings added over time; the Germanic near synonym freedom belongs to a separate history.
intro.cn: 整个家族都依托一个表示自由人的拉丁形容词，随后加上名词、动词与施事后缀；日耳曼语的近义词「自由」属于另一段历史。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the derived adjective for generosity of character.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及由它派生、表示气度宽厚的形容词。

items.meaning: the condition of a free person
items.example: The charter guaranteed the liberty of every citizen.
items.exampleCN: 宪章保障每位公民的自由。

items.meaning: of a free person; generous, open-minded
items.meaningCN: 自由人的；宽厚的、开明的
items.example: A liberal education once meant the studies fit for a free person.
items.exampleCN: 「自由教育」原指适合自由人研习的科目。

items.meaningCN: 宽厚，尤指态度上的宽容
items.example: The host was praised for his liberality.
items.exampleCN: 主人因宽厚而受到称赞。

items.example: The troops liberated the occupied town.
items.exampleCN: 部队解放了被占领的城镇。

items.example: The museum marks the anniversary of the liberation.
The general was hailed as a liberator.
items.exampleCN: 那位将军被称颂为解放者。

items.meaning: one who holds personal freedom to be the highest value
items.meaningCN: 主张个人自由至上的人
items.example: The candidate described himself as a libertarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位候选人自称自由意志论者。

items.example: The measure was criticised as illiberal.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施被批评为不宽容。

items.example: The villagers gave thanks for their deliverance.

latinEntries.meaning: freedom; the status of a free person
